Subject (in full) Reported release of Chen To-seu (陳獨秀), ex-Chief of
the Chinese Trotsky Clique.
Made by D.I. Kuh Tao-hwa Forwarded by D I J Cogan
With reference to the information contained in
the attached report of May 13, 1936, concerning the alleged
appearance in Shanghai of Chen To-seu (陳獨秀), ex- Chief
of the Trotsky Clique of the Chinese Communist Party, about
the middle of May 1936, this report has been emphatically denied
by the Chinese Authorities at Nanking, who declare that Chen
is still detained in the Military Gaol there, serving his term
of 8 years imprisonment.
The original information concerning Chen's alleged
release from the hands of the Chinese Authorities has, in all
probability, derived its origin from Japanese sources.
D.I.R

Subject (in full) Re. Chen To-seu (陈独秀), Chief of the Trotsky Clique,
Chinese Communist Party.

Made by... and ... Forwarded by... D.S.I. Coyne

Information has been received from a reliable source
to the effect that Chen To-seu, Chief of the Trotsky Clique
of the Chinese Communist Party, who was arrested in the
Settlement on behalf of the Chinese Authorities in 1932 and
sentenced to 8 years imprisonment, was seen at large in
Shanghai a few days ago.
A recent report carried by the vernacular press to the
effect that Chen had been transferred to a reformatory was
officially denied, it being stated by the organ concerned
that he was still in gaol.

J Coyne
D. S. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

May 4, 1936.                                          Morning translation.
Sin Wen Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking:-

CHEN TOU SEU TO BE TRANSFERRED TO A REFORMATORY

        Chen Tou Seu was convicted and sentenced in
July 1934 by the Supreme Court on the charge of Offence
against the Internal Security of the State to 8 years
imprisonment, and since that time he has been serving
his term in the First Jail at Soochow. His work in the
prison is to read the proofs of the printing matters.
        In view of the fact that he has observed
the prison regulations, the jail authorities are taking
steps to have him transferred to the Kiangsu Reformatory
until he has completed one-third of his term.

1936年5月4日。 晨间翻译。
《新闻报》刊登如下南京电报：-

陈独秀将被移送感化院

陈独秀于1934年7月因危害国家安全罪被最高法院定罪并判处八年监禁，此后一直在苏州第一监狱服刑。他在狱中的工作是校对印刷品。
鉴于其遵守监狱规章，监狱当局正采取措施，在其服满三分之一刑期前，将其移送江苏感化院。

January 16, 1936. Morning translation.

Shun Pao publishes the following telegram from Nanking:-

CHEN TOU SIU REFUSES TO ENTER ENFORMATORY

Chen Tou Siu (陳獨秀) and Bang Zuh Ts
(彭述之) have served two years in prison.. In view of
the fact that Chen Tou Siu has properly observed the
prison regulations, the authorities intend to transfer
him to the Reformatory in Soochow, but Chen does not want
to go.. His wife Huang Wu Tsoo (黃武初) is willing to
go to Soochow to repent her former misdeeds.

Afternoon Translation - Aug. 23, 1937.

Lih Pao, Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking
telegram) :-

CHEN TU-SIU TO BE RELEASED THIS WEEK

Chen Tu-siu (陈独秀), Communist leader, will
be released this week.
At 3 p.m. August 22, several of his friends from
Peiping University visited him in gaol. Chen stated
that he had decided to devote his life in the interests of
the nation and that after his release he would reside in
Nanking for a short time.

Chen Tu-siu will be released as soon as the
Kiangsu First Gaol receives the order to reduce the term
of imprisonment imposed on him. He will stay at the
Capital for a short time and will interview members of
journalistic circles.

下午翻译 - 1937年8月23日。

《立报》、《新闻晚报》及其他本地报纸（南京电报）：-

陈独秀将于本周获释

共产党领导人陈独秀（陈独秀）将于本周获释。
8月22日下午3时，他的几位北京大学朋友到监狱探望了他。陈表示，他已决定为国效力，获释后将在南京短期居住。

一旦江苏第一监狱收到减刑令，陈独秀即获释放。他将在首都短期停留，并会见新闻界人士。

Extract from Chinese Newspaper Translation.

October 6, 1932.

COMMUNISM.

The "Diamond", a mosquito newspaper.

CHEN TUK SIU JOINS THE KUOMINTANG

After having spent several years closely
investigating general conditions in China, Chen Tuk
Siu(陈独秀), a prominent Communist leftist leader,
recently confessed that Communism can never permanently
exist in China. He now intends to become a follower
of Dr. Sun Yat-sen's Three Peoples Principle and has
joined the ranks of the Kuomintang.

The Central Kuomintang Organ recently offered
him an important post and it is expected in the near
future that he and his staff will become the leading
members of the Kuomintang.

1932年10月6日。

共产主义。

《金刚钻》，一家小型报纸。

陈独秀加入国民党

著名共产党左翼领导人陈独秀（陈独秀）在花费数年时间密切调查中国总体局势后，近日承认共产主义在中国永远无法长久存在。他现在打算成为孙中山博士三民主义的追随者，并已加入国民党行列。

国民党中央机关最近向他提供了一个重要职位，预计在不久的将来，他和他的幕僚将成为国民党的主要领导成员。

( EXTRACT FROM RECORD IN SECTION 2 )

CHEN TO SEU (陈独秀)

Chen To Seu(陈独秀) is a native of Anhwei, born
about 1885. Was formerly a professor of the Peking
University and later a Commissioner of Education in Canton.
Once resided at No. 2 Yu Yang Lee, Route Vallen, French
Concession. Was charged by French Police on 4.10.21 for
being in possession of inflammatory literature and was
fined $100. Arrested again by French Police on 9.8.22
on a similar charge and, in addition to being fined $400.,
was compelled to sign a bond for his future good behaviour.

Head of the Executive Committee of the Bolshevik
Party in China. He directs all the movements of the
Chinese Bolsheviks in accordance with the instructions of
the Eastern Representatives appointed by the 3rd International
at Moscow. Visited Shanghai during the general strike
in 1925. Known to have occasionally lodged in Eh Tseh
Sze(合作社), K.3136 Beane Road, and the printing department
of the Chung Hwa Book Company, Bubbling Well Road.

He was arrested in Peking in Peking in 1919 and
imprisoned for about three months. In 1920 he established
the Sing Tsing Nyl Sze(新青年社)Bookstore, 263 Rue de
Consulat, French Concession, Shanghai,which was closed by
the French Police at the end of the year.

He was in Hankow in 1926 when Southern Army had taken
possession of that territory.

On May 16, 1927, he addressed a meeting in Hankow
urging the co-operation between the revolutionaries of China
and India.

Associated with Borodin and Li Lih San in Hankow,
July, 1927.

Expelled from the Chinese Communist Party in 1927.
------

（特科第二股记录摘录）

陈独秀（陈独秀）

陈独秀（陈独秀）是安徽人，生于1885年左右。曾任北京大学教授，后任广州教育委员会委员。曾居住在法租界瓦伦路（Route Vallen）余阳里2号。1921年10月4日因持有煽动性文献被法国警察指控，罚款100元。1922年8月9日又因类似指控被法国警察逮捕，除罚款400元外，还被责令具结保证日后行为端正。

中国布尔什维克党执行委员会主席。他根据莫斯科第三国际任命的东方代表的指示，指挥中国布尔什维克的所有活动。1925年大罢工期间曾访问上海。已知偶尔寄住在贝恩路（Beane Road）K.3136合作社（Eh Tseh Sze）及静安寺路中华书局印刷部。

他于1919年在北京被捕，监禁约三个月。1920年他在上海法租界领事馆路263号创办新青年社（Sing Tsing Nyl Sze）书店，该书店于年底被法国警察关闭。

1926年南方军队占领该地区时，他在汉口。

1927年5月16日，他在汉口的一次会议上发表讲话，呼吁中国与印度革命者合作。

1927年7月在汉口与鲍罗廷和李立三有联系。

1927年被开除出中国共产党。

Since his expulsion in 1927 from the Chinese Communist
Party, Chen Te Seu has been engaged in work directed against
the Third International and the Central Committee of the
Chinese Communist Party. On account of his advanced age,
however, his activity was of a limited character and has not
brought the results he expected.

Chen Teu Seu formerly published for a certain period a
review in Shanghai entitled "Sin Shiang Dau(新筆鬥)" This
review received a monthly subsidy of $3,000 from an
influential member of the Kuomintang residing in Rue Moliere,
French Concession (probably means Sun Fo who resides at No.10
Rue Moliere).

Chen had two sons. Chen Yen Hyi(陈延年), the elder son,
was an influential member of the Chinese Communist Party
and held the post of Secretary of the Kwangtung Provincial
Committee. He was assassinated in Shanghai in Summer of
1927 when he was Secretary of the Kiangsu and Chekiang
Committee.

The younger son, Chen Jao Hyi(陈乔年) was not so well known
as his brother. In 1928 he was arrested in Shanghai
together with Sung Foh Tar(郑覆他), chairman of the Shanghai
General Labour Union, and Hsu Bah Woo(许白昊), Secretary
General of the Said union. Inspite of Dr. Tsai Yuan Pei's
intervention, Chen Jao Hyi was executed a week after his
arrest. (From the Yung Hua Jih Pao of June 22, 1932).

陈独秀自1927年被中国共产党开除以来，一直从事针对第三国际和中国共产党中央委员会的工作。然而，由于年事已高，他的活动范围有限，并未取得他预期的成果。

陈独秀此前曾在上海出版过一份名为《新笔斗》的刊物。该刊物每月从一位居住在法租界莫利爱路（Rue Moliere）的国民党要员那里获得3,000美元的补贴（此人可能指居住在莫利爱路10号的孙科）。

陈有两个儿子。长子陈延年是中国共产党的要员，曾任广东省委书记。1927年夏，他在担任江苏和浙江委员会书记期间在上海被暗杀。

次子陈乔年不如乃兄知名。1928年，他在上海与上海总工会主席郑覆他及该会秘书长许白昊一同被捕。尽管有蔡元培博士的干预，陈乔年在被捕一周后仍被处决。（摘自1932年6月22日《庸报》）。

June 5, 1931. Afternoon Translation

CONFIDENTIAL

CHEN YOU REN'S ARRIVAL IN HANKOW.

The Shanghai Pao, a mosquito paper, publishes the following article:-
In the Spring of 1928 Chen You Ren returned to China from Moscow. He intended to reorganize the Chinese Communist Party, but he was not recognized by Chiang Kai-shek who was then controlling the Party.
On account of his opposition towards the Soviet and - which - that you can see are financed by Russia. He was also in sympathy with Trotsky who is now in exile.
Labouring under the handicap of financial difficulties rendering him incapable of carrying out his activities in China, Chen You Ren went to Europe in an endeavour to make an alliance with prominent members of the Socialist and Democratic Parties and with their assistance to expand his organization and activities.
Awaiting the start of the second civil war in China, Chen You arrived at Hankow from England on or about May 20, 1931, accompanied by Chen Hao Tien , Lo Shu Hung , Wang Teh Yu and five others. Whilst abroad he had raised about $500,000 with which he intended to continue the reorganization of the Trotsky Party in China. He is said to be staying at the Queen's Hotel, Hankow.

陈友仁抵达汉口。

小报《上海报》刊登了以下文章：-
1928年春，陈友仁从莫斯科返回中国。他意图重组中国共产党，但未得到当时控制该党的蒋介石的认可。
由于他反对苏联——你可以看到，这是由俄国资助的。他还同情目前流亡在外的托洛茨基。
受限于财政困难，导致他无法在中国开展活动，陈友仁前往欧洲，试图与社会主义和民主党派的显要成员结盟，并在他们的帮助下扩大其组织和活动。
等待中国第二次内战爆发之际，陈友于1931年5月20日左右从英国抵达汉口，随行人员有陈浩天、罗书宏、王德宇等五人。他在国外筹集了约50万美元，打算用于继续在中国重组托洛茨基派政党。据说他住在汉口的皇后饭店。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MARCH 7, 1931

SUPPORT OF
CHINA REDS
WITHDRAWN
BY MOSCOW

Internal Confusion Is Said
To Be Cause Of
Party Action

SECRET ADVICES

Financial Aid No Longer
Available, Nanking
Reports Indicate

(Special To The China Press)
Nanking, March 6.—The
Communist Party in China
has lost the support of Moscow, if certain secret advices
reaching here today are true.
The Supreme Council of the
Third International at a recent meeting held in the Soviet capital decided that no
further financial assistance
would be extended to the
party in China in view of the
confusion and disorganization
in the Communist ranks here.

It is stated that Li Li-san, notorious Chinese Communist leader in
a recent report on Red activities
in China, exaggerated the "success"
of his followers in Central China
in their program of destruction.
He was said to have also deliberately minimized the effect of
the actions taken by the Nanking
Government in dealing with the
Reds which have resulted in the
capture and execution of a large
number of important leaders.

Rival Communist leaders of Li
Lih-san have also fanned the flame
of opposition to the once all-powerful Red agitator with the result that many of his personal followers who, up to a few months ago
were holding key positions in the
Chinese Communist Party hierarchy, have also started a movement
to remove Li from his present
exalted post.

Started As Coolie
Li Lili-san started life from a
humble origin. Until ten years
ago, he had no regular occupation,
being variously engaged as a common day laborer. Prior to the
big strike in Shanghai several
years ago, he was said to have
been a wheel-barrow coolie.
The strike gave him the biggest opportunity of his life. Soon
afterwards he was seen riding in
the streets of Shanghai in an expensive limousine of his own. It
was known at the time that he
had joined the Chinese Communist Party and had worked his
way to a high position by virtue
of his recklessness.

When the Communist regime was
set up in Hankow, Li went there
to lend a hand and was regarded
as one of the guiding spirits of
the movement in Central China.

Fled To Peiping
After the collapse of Borodin's
dictatorship, Li, together with the
other important members of the
executive committee of the Chinese Communist Party, fled to Peiping and hid himself in the Soviet
Embassy.
It was from this place that he
did much of the directing of the
Communist activities in the face of
measures taken by the Nanking
authorities for the suppression of
the Reds in China.
Subsequently, he escaped to
Moscow where he is believed to
be living at present.

莫斯科撤回
对中国赤色分子的支持

据称内部混乱
是党采取行动的原因

秘密消息

南京报告显示
不再提供财政援助

（《字林西报》专讯）
南京，3月6日。—如果今天到达这里的某些秘密消息属实，中国共产党已失去莫斯科的支持。
第三国际最高委员会最近在苏联首都举行的一次会议上决定，鉴于此处共产党队伍内部的混乱和无组织状态，不再向中国的党提供进一步的财政援助。

据悉，著名的中国共产党领导人李立三在一份关于中国赤色活动的近期报告中，夸大了其追随者在华中地区破坏计划中的“成功”。据说他还故意淡化南京政府对付赤色分子所采取行动的效果，这些行动导致大量重要领导人被捕并被处决。

李立三的共产党竞争对手也煽动了反对这位曾经权势熏天的赤色煽动者的火焰，结果，许多直到几个月前还在中国共产党层级中占据关键职位的个人追随者，也开始发起运动，将李从其目前的高位上拉下。

出身苦力
李立三出身卑微。直到十年前，他没有固定职业，曾做过各种普通日工。据说在几年前上海大罢工之前，他曾是一名独轮车苦力。
这次罢工给了他一生中最大的机会。不久之后，有人看到他在上海街头乘坐自己拥有的昂贵豪华轿车。当时众所周知，他已加入中国共产党，并凭借鲁莽行事一步步爬到了高位。

当汉口建立共产党政权时，李前往那里助阵，被视为华中运动的指导精神人物之一。

逃往北平
鲍罗廷独裁统治垮台后，李与中国共产党执行委员会的其他重要成员一起逃往北平，并藏身于苏联大使馆。
正是在这个地方，面对南京当局镇压中国赤色分子的措施，他指挥了大量的共产党活动。
随后，他逃往莫斯科，据信目前居住在那里。

REPORT
Date January 27, 1931.

Subject (in full) Whereabouts of Li Lih-san (李立三) and Chen To-seu (陳獨秀).

Made by D. I. Robertson Forwarded by [Signature: Jno Robertson]

With reference to the attached memorandum re
"Change in Policy of Moscow causes Split among Chinese
Communists", inquiries have failed to elicit any
information that either Li Lih-san (李立三) or Chen
To-seu (陳獨秀) is at present in Shanghai.

The following paragraph is an extract from the
Intelligence Report of January 6, 1931, and so far no
information has been received to discredit it.

"It is reported that Moscow is dissatisfied
with Li Lih-san (李立三), the notorious communistic
leader, and his clique and has accordingly called him
to Russia to undergo further training. It is also
reported that one Chang Kuo-tao (張國燾) has been
sent from Moscow to Shanghai to reorganize C.P. Central
and another named Ku Meng-yu (顧孟餘) to reorganize the
Kiangsu Branch."

Chang Kuo-tao (張國燾) mentioned above has
not come to notice previously nor has his arrival here
been detected.

It is also significant that in all the literature
seized during the series of raids on communistic bases
carried out between January 17 and 21, 1931 no reference
to the presence of Li Lih-san (李立三) or Chen To-seu
(陳獨秀) in Shanghai is made.

It is also noteworthy that the Nanking Government
has offered a reward of $10,000.00 for the arrest of
either one of the said leaders, which has resulted in
strenuous efforts on the part of Nanking's informers to
locate them.

[Signature: Henry Robertson]
D. I.

D. C. (Cr. & Sp. Branches).
Information. I shall inform S.
28.1.'31.

主题（全称）李立三和陈独秀的下落。

制作人 D. I. Robertson 转发人 [签名：Jno Robertson]

关于附件中题为“莫斯科政策变更导致中国共产党分裂”的备忘录，经查询，未能获得任何关于李立三或陈独秀目前在上海的信息。

以下段落摘录自1931年1月6日的情报报告，截至目前，未收到任何信息证明其不实。

“据报道，莫斯科对臭名昭著的共产党领导人李立三及其派系感到不满，因此召他回俄国接受进一步训练。另据报道，张国焘已从莫斯科派往上海重组中共中央，另一人顾孟余则负责重组江苏分部。”

上述提到的张国焘此前未曾引起注意，也未发现其抵达此地。

同样值得注意的是，在1931年1月17日至21日期间对共产党据点的一系列突袭中查获的所有文献中，均未提及李立三或陈独秀在上海的存在。

此外，值得注意的是，南京政府已悬赏10,000.00美元逮捕上述任一领导人，这导致南京的情报人员极力寻找他们的下落。

January 15, 1931. REC.

15 - 1 - 31.

The following memorandum is based on information obtained
from a very reliable source:-

Change in Policy of Moscow causes Split among
Chinese Communists.

The Soviet Government and III International have for
many years been spending considerable sums of money on the
promotion of social unrest in various countries. The bulk of
this money has been expended to propagate Communism and the
balance has been used to exploit elements of disorder with
a view to causing trouble for capitalist countries. The
Soviet Government has reversed its ideas in regard to the
respective importance of the objectives mentioned, and has
now decided to devote the bulk of the money appropriated for
propaganda abroad to the promotion and fostering of sentiments
and movements hostile to the so-called Imperialist nations.

It is expected that this change of policy will result in
Soviet energy in China being concentrated in creating and
extending agitation hostile to the Powers enjoying extra-
territoriality, such as, demands for the restoration of
concessions, requests for the abolition of extraterritoriality
and appeals to the Government for enforcement of changes in the
educational system which will be prejudicial to missionary
efforts.

The instruments to be used to give effect to the new
policy in China will include Anti-Imperialist Leagues, Oppressed
People's Associations and other societies which preserve
themselves against Government interference by masquerading as
patriotic organizations.

As a result of the change in the policy of Moscow,
the Chinese Communist groups have split into two parties.
One set of groups, of which Li Lih San(李立山) is chief,
favours the maintenance of the old affiliations with Moscow

1931年1月15日。收件。

以下备忘录基于从非常可靠的来源获得的信息：-

莫斯科政策变更导致中国共产党分裂。

苏联政府和第三国际多年来一直在花费巨额资金促进各国的社会动荡。这笔资金的大部分用于宣传共产主义，其余部分用于利用混乱因素，旨在给资本主义国家制造麻烦。苏联政府已逆转了关于上述目标各自重要性的想法，现在决定将拨给海外宣传的大部分资金用于促进和培育敌视所谓帝国主义国家的情绪和运动。

预计这一政策变化将导致苏联在华精力集中于制造和扩展敌视享有治外法权列强的煽动活动，例如要求归还租界、请求废除治外法权以及呼吁政府实施将对传教工作产生不利影响的教育制度改革。

在中国实施新政策的工具将包括反帝同盟、被压迫民族协会以及其他通过伪装成爱国组织来规避政府干涉的社团。

由于莫斯科政策的改变，中国共产党团体分裂为两派。其中一派以李立山为首，主张维持与莫斯科

and the III International. The groups comprising the

will operate independent of Moscow.
A reaction of the power of the Chinese Communists
resulting from the split has been aggravated through
attempts, made by the various Communist groups to get
together and decide upon a future policy, having failed
in consequence of the vigilance of the authorities of the
different places in which the delegates of the Party
had planned to assemble.
The leaders of the present rival sets of groups
in the Chinese Communist Party, Li Lih San and Chen To Seu,
are said to be hiding in Shanghai at present.

由于各共产党团体试图聚集在一起决定未来政策的尝试失败——这是因为当局对党代表计划集结的不同地点保持了警惕——导致中国共产党势力因分裂而受到的削弱进一步加剧。

warrant and the warrant and accompanied by the representative of the
Shanghai Public Safety Bureau the police raided a house at No.210
Tshung Yang Li off East Yuhang Road at 2.55p.m. on the 15.10.32. In
the upstairs front room they arrested the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th
accused. These five accused are the members of the Standing Committee
of the Chinese Communist Party. The 1st Accused admitted that he
was conducting a meeting for the 6th accused who was sick at the time.

moved to the Police Hospital for examination. When the 4th accused
was questioned he stated that he lives at No.622 Rua Foo Li off Route
des Soeurs, so the police with the assistance rendered by the French
police raided the premises and arrested the 7th accused. At. 12.50am
on the 16.10.32 the police raided a house at No.1044 S 'ung Li off Ta-
tung Road. They met a little difficulty before obtaining their en-
trance. When they got in they were just in time to see two men jump-
ing out through a window. One of the detectives followed them and he
subsequently succeeded in the arrest of the 8th accused. (8th Accused
being one of the two men who jumped out of the window) At about 7.20
p.m. on the 16.10.32 they also raided house No.335 Nyin Kwong Li off
Tongshan Road and arrested the 9th and 10th Accused. Later they ra-
ided a house At No.22, Passage No.456 off Rue Frelupt and there the

第 2 名被告回答法官：- 我曾是南京东南大学（Tun' Nan ' college）的学生。离校后我北上找工作，但未成功，未能找到任何性质的工作。当时我年仅 20 岁。之后我回到了安徽老家。我在那里待了接下来的四（4）年。这段时间我一直没有工作。因此我与任何共产党派别都没有关联。我不认识第 6 名被告，但我经朋友介绍认识了第 1 名被告。我不知道任何党派领导人的名字。我认识这第 1 名被告仅一周时间。我不能说他是否与激进党派有任何关联。

法官对第 2 名被告说：- 如果是这样，那此人怎么会指控你是该党派的一员呢？

第 2 名被告回答主审法官：- 如果是那样，那他就是在诬陷我。作为一名学生，我不是任何此类党派的成员。我当时的想法是成为一名好农民，为此我致力于我的学业。我承认我与这些其他被告一起被捕，但对于警方当时查获的书籍，我一无所知。这些箱子都是锁着的。

第 3 名被告：- 我曾是宝隆学院（Pao Zung ' college）的学生。我去过俄罗斯，并在那里学习了两（2）年。我于 1921 年去俄罗斯，于 1924 年回家。在此之前，我也是上海学院（Shanghai college）的学生。我于 1921 年加入该党，并从那天起成为一名共产主义者。我是河南人，我自愿加入了这个共产党

出于我个人的自由意志。我现在向其他新同志传授这一运动的理想。至于我们的总部，我们在上海或国内其他地方都没有固定的地点。我不打算回答法官提出的涉及党的领导层或我们称为总部的地方的问题，我不会回答涉及这一方面的任何问题。如果法官提出他认为合适的问题，只要不牵连他人且在我能力范围内，我会回答。我不会回答任何涉及党的档案的问题。我于 1921 年成为该党成员。我不愿谈论“托洛茨基”或左翼反对派集团。那是他所属的党派。1924 年去世的领袖“列宁”也是该党的领袖。我也是该党的成员。我不愿泄露任何党员的姓名。关于第 6 名被告，我不愿回答任何问题。是的，他也是该党的领导人。我也是行政党的成员。我和第 6 名被告以及另一名未被拘留的人是党的主要成员。我不愿向法官做任何特别陈述。我只回答法官直接提出的问题。我说我们只有三名行政机构成员。从字面意义上讲，我不是罪犯。法律对我唯一的指控是我持有不同的政府观点，因此我的罪行不过是政治性的。如果本国政府因这一罪行判处我死刑，我对此无话可说。在回答他们向我提出的任何问题时，我将只为自己作答，不涉及其他人。我承认我是一名共产主义者；如果结果是死亡，我也不畏惧。

法官对第三被告说：我有几个问题要问你，但时间紧迫，我还有其他人要审问。
第三被告回答法官：我会回答这位法官提出的任何问题。除了我对本国政府持有不同观点外，我没有犯下其他罪行。我们所属的党派与其他此类党派不同，因为我们是“反对派系”。
法官对第三被告说：根据你对这场运动的看法，共产主义运动的最终结果会是什么？
第三被告回答法官：要充分回答这个问题需要很多时间，但主要思想是这样的。我们要求所有人享有平等权利。我们的目标还包括削弱地主的力量，以及削弱富人掌握的财富权力。为所有失业者提供就业机会。如果我们能做到这一点，手段就能证明目的的正当性。我们的目标还包括推翻中国现政府，代之以一个人人享有平等权利的民治政府。孙中山博士只为他所属的党派而战，但我们为包括穷人在内的所有人民而战。看看山东和满洲里的三千万人，他们对生活没有未来的希望。目前该党还没有推翻政府的计划。随着时间的推移，全国的农民和其他工人会像我们现在这样看待此事，然后他们都会为了同一个目的联合起来。随着时间的推移，世界会像我们一样看待此事并变得共产主义化。我在过去（4）四年里一直是党员。我不能告诉法官党的总指挥部设在哪里。我拒绝透露。当然，我们有

Judge t the 3rd accused:- Is there to be any demonstration
in the near future ? or is there to be any rebellion against the
Government in the near future. ?

3rd accused:- In reply to that I am not in the position to
answer . The Judge will see that at present everything is quiet .
Part of my work is to compose the Books and the Literature of the
party as also the story books . The time for the rebellion has not
yet arrived. I am not able to explain how it is that the police
were able to get their information on which we were arrested; I do
not know How that came about. I knew that from day to day I stood
in danger of this. That is one of the dangers we have to face in
our cause. This was all denied at the police station and the
statements we made there are not the truth. The 6th accused and I
are old friends and we worked together in this case/. I have a wife
and a family and also my parents are still alive. I have spoken
to them all of my views in this respect and none of them will
entertain my ideas. They all object to my views.

4th accused in reply to the Judge:- I was in Japan as a
Student and returned to Shanghai in the 18th year of the Republic
of China. I am not a member of the Koumintang party neither am
I a member of the Communist party. To my knowledge there are only
one or two of these accused who are in any way connected with the
communist endeavour. If they have implicated me then I have been
falsely implicated . I have nothing to say in the case if I have
been implicated by any of the other accused. I do not know the
1st accused neither do I know where he resides. I do not know the
6th accused either . The 1st accused is a very bad man and he may
have implicated me in this . I did not attend any of their meetings
in the 'Tahung Yang Dec Li off the Last Yuhang Road . I went there
there to see one named Tsung Zou Wei ' I am employed at the China
Merchants from 8.am until 5.pm daily.

法官对第三被告说：近期是否会有任何示威活动？或者近期是否会有针对政府的叛乱？

第三被告：对此我无法回答。法官可以看到，目前一切都很平静。我的部分工作是编写党的书籍和文献，以及故事书。叛乱的时机尚未到来。我无法解释警方是如何获得导致我们被捕的情报的；我不知道这是怎么发生的。我知道我每天都处于这种危险之中。这是我们在事业中必须面对的危险之一。这一切在警察局都被否认了，我们在那里所做的陈述并非事实。第六被告和我是老朋友，我们在此案中一起工作。我有妻子和家人，我的父母也健在。我已向他们所有人表达了我在这方面的观点，但他们都不接受我的想法。他们都反对我的观点。

第四被告回答法官：我曾作为学生在日本留学，并于中华民国十八年回到上海。我不是国民党党员，也不是共产党员。据我所知，这些被告中只有一两个人与共产主义活动有任何关联。如果他们牵连了我，那我就是被诬陷的。如果我被其他任何被告牵连，我对此案无话可说。我不认识第一被告，也不知道他住在哪里。我也不认识第六被告。第一被告是个很坏的人，他可能因此牵连了我。我没有参加他们在最后余杭路附近的“大杨德里”（音译）举行的任何会议。我去那里是为了见一个叫宗佐伟（音译）的人。我每天从上午8点到下午5点在招商局工作。

school as a teacher. I have also been a teacher in Canton. At
the time of the Communist uprising in Canton I was residing in

which I was the leader. That was in 1929. There were five (5)
administrative members of that party. At one time the headquarters
of the party were in Shanghai on the Bubblingwell Road but these
have since been removed. The 1st accused is one of the writers

第五被告回答法官：我曾是曾头（音译）中学的学生。我是在第一被告的家中被捕的。我并非那里的居民。是一个我认识的同乡带我到那所房子的。他带我去那里，是因为我想向他说我在那里能找到的人借些钱。这是我第一次去那所房子。我既不认识第一被告，也不认识第六被告。我不是该党的成员。

法官对第五被告说：如果是这样，为什么第六被告要牵连你？

第五被告回答法官：我不明白。是我的朋友带我去那里，向他说我在那里能找到的人借些钱。这就是事实。我没有别名。

（批注：第六被告是 Chow To Sau。Ml.）

第六被告回答法官：在中华民国七年和八年期间，我是一名学校教师。在国民党成立之前，我就成为了共产党员。在中华民国十一年，我成为了共产党员。由国民党执政的现政府是一个非常糟糕的政府，对穷人没有任何帮助。我曾在一所小学校任教。我也曾在广州当过老师。在广州共产党起义期间，我居住在上海。总的来说，我在警察局所做的陈述是正确的。我在那里做的少数几项陈述被错误翻译了。从192...年到1927年，我是党的首席秘书。后来我们成立了反政府党，我是其领导人。那是在1929年。该党有五（5）名行政成员。有一次，党的总部设在上海的静安寺路（Bubblingwell Road），但此后已搬迁。第一被告是该组织的撰稿人之一

of the organisation. I do not know the 2nd or the 6th accused.

7th accused in reply to the Judge:- I am a graduate of the

incriminating, I am not to be held responsible for the actions of
my friends. I ask the police at the station after my arrest for

第六被告回答法官：这个我说不上来：我们尚未与广西共产党联合。我不知道警方是如何发现我们的，也不知道我们是如何被捕的。我曾在北平被捕过一次，并在公安局被拘留了一个月。政府的法律与共产党的法律是不同的。如果法官今天不结案，我请求将我送回医院，因为我仍然病得很重。

第七被告回答法官：我是北平民学院的毕业生，我不是共产党员或国民党党员。我不知道自己做了什么导致被捕，我去第一被告家是为了看望一位朋友，就在我在那里时，警察来了，我和其他被告一起被捕。我去那里是为了看望第四被告。我们曾是同学。我不知道他是否是共产党员。我知道第四被告品行良好，且曾是日本一所学校的学生。警察去了我家并进行搜查，但没有发现任何罪证。我不应为朋友的行为承担责任。被捕后，我在警察局请求允许打电话给律师，但他们拒绝让我这样做。

to the handing over of the accused to the Shanghai Public Safety
Bureau.

Pres: Judge:- In reply to the 3rd accused:- This is not a
case of the police preferring charges against any of you but it is
an application made by the S.P.S.Bureau for the handing over of
all the accused for investigations. You will be handed over and
be brought before the Court for trial tomorrow at . .M.

4th accused to the Judge:- This Court has had the case for
enquiries since this morning and I now ask that the Court inform
my Lawyer of the facts of this case and tell him that the case is
to come up for trial in the morning.

Pres: Judge:- When the case comes for trial at the Bureau
then you may see about the lawyer for thedefence, This Court is also
a Chinese Court and I have the power to order that you be handed
over, as I have heard the evidence against you and as I think
that this evidence is sufficient to warrant your handing over that
is all I am concerned with for the present,

11th accused :- I now ask that this Court order that I be
released as I have nothing to do with the case as against the
accused.

Pres: Judge in reply:- That is for the Shanghai Public Safety
Bureau to decide .

租界内被租界警察逮捕的，现在仅凭 .......Becauthis（原文不清）本庭即将把我们移交，却未对我们任何人指名指控，也未提出针对我的证据。

第三被告：- 这些被告没有犯下违反国家法律的任何罪行；应给予他们聘请辩护律师的机会。但这并未 granted（给予）任何被告。此外，我告知本庭，如果有任何针对我们的案件，应在将被告移交给上海市公安局之前，在本庭进行审理。

主审法官：- 回答第三被告：- 这不是警方对你们任何人提出指控的案件，而是上海市公安局申请将所有被告移交以进行调查。你们将被移交，并于明天上午 . . 点出庭受审。

第四被告对法官说：- 本庭从今天早上开始一直对此案进行讯问，我现在请求法庭将此案事实告知我的律师，并告诉他此案将于明早开庭审理。

主审法官：- 当案件在公安局开庭审理时，你可以去联系辩护律师。本庭也是中国法庭，我有权命令将你们移交，因为我已听取了对你们的证据，且我认为这些证据足以证明将你们移交是正当的，这就是我目前所关注的全部事项，

第十一被告：- 我现在请求本庭命令释放我，因为我与针对被告的案件无关。

主审法官回答：- 这由上海市公安局决定。

Case No. 5/73402-1. Sheet No. 16

9th accused to the Pres: Judge:- If the Government wanted
our arrest why did they wait for us to come to Shanghai and then
have us arrested in the Settlement by the Settlement police and
then to be handed over to them for trial. ? This Government
could have arrested us themselves had they so wanted.?

4th accused to the Pres: Judge:- The Chinese authorities
have nothing against us and we were all arrested in the Settlement.
Why does this Court hand us over if this Court has the power
to deal with the case ? The case should be tried in this Court.

7th accused to the Pres: Judge:- I ask the Court under what
article of the Code we are to be tried and charged ?

Pres: Judge in reply to the 7th accused:- This is an appli-
cation for your handing over and at present there are no charges
preferred against you . Evidence sufficient to warrant this handing
over to the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau has been produced and
therefore you will be handed over in accordance with this applica-
tion from the Bureau.

7th accused in reply to the Judge:- There is no warrant for my
arrest. The police arrested me on the off chance that I may have
been also concerned in the case against the other accused and I
have not been given the chance to protect myself . I now speak in
order that I may be afforded that opportunity. There is no warrant
issued for my arrest.

Pres: Judge in reply to the 7th accused:- This warrant gives
the names of some and states that there are ten others to be
arrested together with the 1st accused .

6th accused:- I ask that the Court take Jurisdiction in the
case against us. ?

Pres: Judge:- In reply to the 6th accused:- You will be handed
over to the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau and there you will be
given a fair trial at which time you can explain the case to the
Court there.

案件编号 5/73402-1。页码 16

第九被告对主审法官说：- 如果政府想要逮捕我们，为什么等我们来到上海，然后由租界警察在租界内逮捕我们，再移交给他们审判？如果政府愿意，他们本可以自行逮捕我们。

第四被告对主审法官说：- 中国当局对我们没有任何指控，我们全都是在租界内被捕的。如果本庭有权处理此案，为何要将我们移交？此案应在本庭审理。

第七被告对主审法官说：- 我请问法庭，我们将依据法典哪一条款受审和被指控？

主审法官回答第七被告：- 这是一项移交你们的申请，目前尚未对你们提出任何指控。已提出足以证明将你们移交给上海市公安局是正当的证据，因此将根据该局的申请将你们移交。

第七被告回答法官：- 没有逮捕我的 warrant（逮捕令）。警察逮捕我是出于一种侥幸心理，认为我可能也牵涉到其他被告的案件中，而我未被给予自我保护的机会。我现在发言是为了获得那个机会。没有签发逮捕我的 warrant。

主审法官回答第七被告：- 这份 warrant 列出了一些人的姓名，并指出还有十人将与第一被告一并逮捕。

第六被告：- 我请求法庭对针对我们的案件行使管辖权。

主审法官：- 回答第六被告：- 你们将被移交给上海市公安局，在那里你们将获得公正的审判，届时你们可以向那里的法庭解释案情。

4th Accused to the res: Judge:- I ask that this Court take

3rd accused:- If this Court in the first place intended that
we were to be handed over to the Bureau why did the Court waste
all this time in questioning these accused.? What kind of Law
is this . ?
res: Judge to the 3rd accused:- warrant was issued on behalf
of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau through the Settlement police
who at the request of this Bureau arrested the accused. This Court
held an investigation into the facts of the case as presented by
the Bureau and now I consider that the facts warrant the handing
over of you all for trial by the City authorities. This Dispatch
states that the 1st accused with ten (10) others are wanted for
investigation and trial.
( At this part of the hearing all the accused strongly
objected to being handed over to the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau )
4th accused to the res: Judge:- This Court has not the right
- to order that we be handed over on such flimsy evidence as
has been offered by the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau.
Mr Lee:- The police of the Settlement arrested these acc:
on the warrant applied for at the request of the Shanghai Public
Safety Bureau. At the same place as were these accused arrested
the police also seized a quantity of Inflammatory literature.
The Government had also issued a circular warrant for the arrest
of the 1st accused and the others of his party. These accused
have committed offences outside the Settlement Limits and should be
handed over to the Bureau for trial for such offences. Some of
these accused have engaged Counsel and if this Counsel failed to
appear at Court it is not the fault of the Court or of the Police
but of the accused.

第四被告对主审法官说：- 我请求本庭对此案行使管辖权，因为我们全都是在租界内被本租界的警察逮捕的。我提出此请求，同时请求允许我们聘请辩护律师。
第三被告：- 如果本庭起初就打算将我们移交给该局，为什么法庭浪费这么多时间讯问这些被告？这是什么法律？
主审法官对第三被告说：- warrant 是代表上海市公安局通过租界警察签发的，租界警察应该局请求逮捕了被告。本庭对该局提交的案件事实进行了调查，现在我认为事实足以证明将你们所有人移交给市政府当局审判是正当的。这份公文指出，第一被告及其他十人需要接受调查和审判。
（在听证会的这一部分，所有被告强烈反对被移交给上海市公安局）
第四被告对主审法官说：- 本庭无权依据上海市公安局提供的如此薄弱的证据命令将我们移交。
李先生：- 租界警察是根据上海市公安局的申请凭 warrant 逮捕了这些被告。在逮捕这些被告的同一地点，警方还查获了大量煽动性文献。政府也已签发通缉令逮捕第一被告及其同党。这些被告在租界范围外犯了罪，应移交给该局以此类罪行受审。部分被告已聘请律师，如果律师未出庭，这不是法庭或警方的过错，而是被告的过错。

ings

罗先生代表警方出庭。

裁决。
由二房东暂时保管，待法庭致函上海市公安局，向囚犯梁月广查询谁可以认领该财产。

July 25, 1933.    Morning Translation

MISCELLANEOUS

The callers were informed by Mr. O.K.Yu,
Chief Secretary of the Municipality, that the matter was
under consideration. The representatives stated that
the 100,000 policy holders would struggle hard against
the insurance companies.

China Times and other local newspapers:

LOTTERIES BY TOBACCO COMPANIES PROHIBITED.

The promotion by various local tobacco
companies of lotteries for cash prizes encourages the
public to smoke and arouses in them sentiments of luck.
The Municipality of Greater Shanghai has
issued instructions to the Bureau of Social Affairs
to place a ban on these lotteries.
The Bureau of Social Affairs has transmitted
the above instructions to the various tobacco companies
concerned. In future, the issue of lottery tickets
offering cash prizes will be prohibited.

China Times and other local newspapers:

HEALTH DEPARTMENT OFFICER CHARGED WITH EXTORTION.

On the afternoon of July 21, Chen Feng (陳逢),
an inspector of the Branch Office of the Health Department
on Shanhaikwan Road, went to the Hsin Fah Shing (新發兴)
Cold Drinks Shop at No.669 North Chengtu Road and
extorted from the owner of the shop a sum of $50.
He was arrested and detained by the police and
was charged in the First Special District Court with
extortion. The sum of $50 was produced to the Court.
Sentence will be passed on Friday.

COMMUNISM

THE CHEN TOU SEU CASE.

The China Times publishes the following letter
from its Soochow Correspondent:-
Acting on instructions received on July 24
from the Supreme Court, which has accepted the appeal
submitted by Chen Tou Seu, Bang Zuh Ts and others against
the sentences passed on them, the Soochow High Court has
detailed a Court official to take the complete file of
the case to Nanking.

C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 4131
Afternoon Translation 5/33）

COMMUNISM

China Times published the following comment on April 30:

THE CHEN TOU SEU CASE.

Chen Tou Seu, a former professor of the Peking
University during the time of Dr. Tsai Yuen Pei's
administration, has been sentenced to 13 years' imprisonment
for disseminating Communism. It is said that Chen will
make an appeal.

Whether Chen Tou Seu is a Communist or whether
he had propagated Communism with the object of endangering
the Republic of China can be judged only through the many
proofs gathered by the authorities. When the Government
carried out the purification movement several years ago,
Wu Shih Huei, a member of the Central Executive Committee
of the Kuomintang, said: "I asked Chen Tou Seu to agree
to let the Kuomintang control Government affairs for twenty
years; after which period we shall talk about the Communist
Party. But Chen agreed to permit the Kuomintang to rule
the country for two years only."

From this statement, one knows that Chen Tou Seu
was unanimously recognised at that time as a leader of the
Communist Party. For this reason, the sentence of 13 years'
imprisonment passed on Chen Tou Seu is quite lenient.

LABOUR

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

INDUSTRIALISTS FORMING INDUSTRIAL WELFARE ASSOCIATION.

In view of the frequent occurrence of accidents
in various factories, certain prominent industrialists in
this locality are organising a body to be known as the
Industrial Welfare Association to look after safety and
sanitary devices in factories and the welfare of workers.
A preparatory meeting of the new Association will be held
on May 6 at No. 360 Rue Paul Beau, French Concession.

A general outline of the work of the Association
is as follows:-
1) To supervise and to conduct research into the safety,
sanitary and other devices in local factories.
2) To introduce and to improve safety and sanitary devices
in factories.
3) To publish periodicals, deliver lectures, hold exhibitions
and distribute books containing pictures, slogans and
other propaganda articles on the various industries.

It is reported that the Association will publish
an Industrial Safety Monthly Magazine. The first issue
will appear on June 1.

1933年5月下午译文）

共产主义

《时报》于4月30日发表以下评论：

陈独秀案。

陈独秀，蔡元培博士任职期间的北京大学前教授，因传播共产主义被判刑13年。据悉，陈将提出上诉。

陈独秀是否是共产党员，或者他是否以危害中华民国为目的传播共产主义，只能通过当局收集的许多证据来判断。当政府在几年前开展清党运动时，国民党中央执行委员会委员吴稚晖（Wu Shih Huei）说：“我请陈独秀同意让国民党控制政府事务二十年；期满后我们再谈论共产党。但陈只同意让国民党统治国家两年。”

从这番话可知，陈独秀当时被一致公认为共产党领袖。因此，判处陈独秀13年徒刑是相当宽大的。

劳工

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

实业家组建工业福利协会。

鉴于各工厂事故频发，本地一些著名实业家正在组织一个名为“工业福利协会”的团体，以负责工厂的安全和卫生设施以及工人的福利。新协会的筹备会议将于5月6日在法租界贝当路360号举行。

协会工作大纲如下：
1) 监督和研究本地工厂的安全、卫生及其他设施。
2) 引进和改进工厂的安全和卫生设施。
3) 出版期刊、举办讲座、举行展览，并发行包含图片、标语和其他关于各行业宣传文章的书籍。

据报道，该协会将出版《工业安全月刊》。第一期将于6月1日发行。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 4131
Date 1 / 5 / 33

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, MAY 1, 1933

Liberties Group
Protests Terms
For Trotskyist

Views Contrary To Those
Of Ruling Powers Held
Not Criminal Offense

Chen Said Convicted
Only On His Writings

The China League for Civil Rights passed the following manifesto yesterday:

"The China League for Civil Rights protests against the sentence to imprisonment varying from 13 years to two years and six months which was passed upon Chen Tu-hsiu, Peng Shu-tse and other so-called 'political' prisoners on the sole evidence of having written by the Kiangsu High Court on April 26. It wishes to point out that the condemned, being Trotskyites, were never charged with acts of violence or with connection with the anti-Japanese agitation in Shanghai, but were found guilty only of publishing writings which were considered as 'propaganda against the Republic.' It wishes to point out further that Professor Ma Chen-ming and Han Yu-lan of Peiping were also sentenced to imprisonment for one year and six months merely on the strength of their lectures below.

'It seems incredible that, during the present national crisis, when the government is in face of external aggression and internal bankruptcy, should it be best to increase the living force of the nation, it should choose to start a persecution last December of political writers as if they were the real method of mobilizing the national attention. With the special characteristic of the Kuomintang regime, censorship has become a crime in both political opinions. A written expression of the popular party, or to define the people's rights means at least an attempt to have some sort of self-government. The press is not free to express its views. The people are not free to express their views. The government is not free to express its views. The people are not free to express their views. The government is not free to express its views.

'The league wishes to call attention to the fact that the holding of heterodox political beliefs is not a crime in modern civilized countries. The fact that there are people in Kiangsi and Hopeh who have taken arms against the government is no reason for suppressing the civil rights of the whole nation, namely the right of free belief, free speech, free press, free assembly and the right of protection of person and property. Once freedom of these is gone, To-day and the coming generation are to stand in every part of our country, and the country's prisons are full of people who are suspected in defense of individual rights or many more or all political parties opposed to the ruling party. The suppression and persecution of thought have so drastic, so thorough and so rampant.

'The China League for Civil Rights demands the immediate release of all political prisoners including Professor Ma and Han, Chen Tu-hsiu and the other seven prominent defendants with him. It demands that the Chinese people should have their constitutional rights respected and protected. It appeals to the nation to rally round this fight for their civil rights as the only way to liberate the living forces of the nation.'

see "League" and
cross "under"
under China League
for Civil Rights.

自由派团体
抗议对托洛茨基主义者的
判决条款

持有与执政当局相左之观点
不构成刑事犯罪

陈氏称其仅因文字作品
而被定罪

中国民权保障同盟昨日通过如下宣言：

“中国民权保障同盟抗议江苏高等法院于4月26日仅凭写作行为这一单一证据，便判处陈独秀、彭述之及其他所谓‘政治’犯十三年至两年六个月不等的监禁刑期。本同盟谨指出，受刑者身为托洛茨基主义者，从未被指控实施暴力行为或与上海的反日 agitation（运动/骚动）有关联，其被判有罪仅仅是因为发表了被视为‘反对民国宣传’的文字作品。本同盟进一步指出，北平的马哲民教授和韩幽兰女士也仅因其下述演讲内容而被判处一年六个月监禁。

‘令人难以置信的是，在当前国家危机之际，政府面临外敌侵略和内部破产，本应致力于增强国家的生命力，却选择从去年十二月开始迫害政治作家，仿佛这才是动员国民注意力的真正方法。鉴于国民党政权的特殊性，审查制度使得政治观点的表达本身成为一种罪行。书面表达民众的意愿，或者界定人民的权利，至少意味着尝试某种形式的自治。新闻界无法自由表达其观点。人民无法自由表达其观点。政府无法自由表达其观点。人民无法自由表达其观点。政府无法自由表达其观点。

‘本同盟提请注意这样一个事实：在现代文明国家中，持有异端政治信仰并非犯罪。江西和河北有人武装对抗政府，这不能成为压制全国公民权利的理由，即信仰自由、言论自由、出版自由、集会自由以及人身和财产受保护的权利。一旦这些自由丧失，当今及后代将遍布我国各地，而国家的监狱里将挤满因捍卫个人权利或属于反对执政党的许多乃至所有政党而受嫌疑的人。对思想的压制和迫害是如此严厉、如此彻底且如此猖獗。

‘中国民权保障同盟要求立即释放所有政治犯，包括马教授和韩女士、陈独秀及其同案的其他七名主要被告。本同盟要求中国人民的宪法权利得到尊重和保护。本同盟呼吁全国人民团结起来，为争取民权而战，这是解放国家生命力的唯一途径。’”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES. FRIDAY, APRIL 28, 1933

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. D Date / / ）

LEADER OF TROTSKY
GROUP IN CHINA

13 Years' Imprisonment
For Chen Tu-hsiu
And Henchman

NANKING, April 27.—Judgment in the case of Chen Tu-hsiu, leader of the Trotsky faction of the Chinese Communist Party, and nine other alleged Communists, was announced by the Kiangning (Nanking) District Court yesterday.

Both Chen Tu-hsiu and his henchman, Peng Shih-chih, were found guilty of disseminating seditious propaganda and were each sentenced to 13 years' imprisonment and deprivation of civic rights for 15 years.

Six other accused were also convicted and sentenced as follows:—

Wang Tzu-ping and Ho Ah-ang; 5 years' imprisonment and deprivation of civic rights for 7 years for aiding and abetting in the dissemination of seditious propaganda.

Wang Tu, Po I-fan, and Wang Chao-chun: 5 years' imprisonment and deprivation of civic rights for 7 years, for the formation of organizations with the object of subverting the Republic.

Kuo Ching-hao: 2½ year's imprisonment and deprivation of civic rights for 3 years, for formation of organizations with the object of subverting the Republic. (He was given a lighter sentence because of mitigating circumstances).

Two of the accused, namely, Liang Yu-kwang and Wang Chien-tang, were acquitted.

All of the convicted prisoners have indicated their intention to appeal against the decision of the Court.—Kuo Min.

中国托洛茨基
派别领袖

陈独秀及其
亲信获刑13年

南京，4月27日电。— 江宁（南京）地方法院昨日宣布了对中国共产党托洛茨基派领袖陈独秀及其他九名涉嫌共产主义者的案件判决。

陈独秀及其亲信彭述之均被裁定犯有散布煽动性宣传罪，各被判处监禁13年，并剥夺公权15年。

另外六名被告也被定罪并判决如下：—

王子平和何阿芳；因协助和教唆散布煽动性宣传，判处监禁5年，剥夺公权7年。

王武、濮一凡和王兆群：因组建旨在颠覆共和国的组织，判处监禁5年，剥夺公权7年。

郭清浩：因组建旨在颠覆共和国的组织，判处监禁2年半，剥夺公权3年。（因情节较轻，予以从轻处罚）。

两名被告，即梁有光和王锦堂，被宣告无罪。

所有已定罪的囚犯均表示有意对法院判决提出上诉。—《国民新闻》。

China Times (Nanking telegram):

THE CHEN TOU SEU CASE.

The Nanking District Court delivered the following
judgment in the Chen Tou Seu case yesterday:-

Chen Tou Seu and Bang Jih Ts have been sentenced
to 13 years' imprisonment and 15 years' deprivation of civil
rights on a charge of subverting the Government with written
propaganda.

Wang Wu (王武), Pu Yih Van (濮一凡) and Wang Zau
Kyuin (王兆群) have been sentenced to two and half years'

on a charge of founding organizations with the object of
endangering the Republic.

Liang Yu Kwang (梁有光) and Wang Kying Tang (王錦堂)

Chen and Bang were allowed to read books and to
receive callers in prison.

Chen is considering an appeal against the sentence.

Q 4131
5801
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, APRIL 22, 1933

Chen Tu-hsiu
Trial Ends,
Verdict 26th

Trotskyist Cites He
Employed Only Words
In Opposing Nanking

Opposing Tanguu Said
Not Opposing State

NANKING, Apr. 21.—(Reuter)—
The trial of Chen Tu-hsiu, leader of
the Trotsky faction of the Chinese
Communist Party, and nine other
alleged Communists, was resumed
at the Jiangsu District Court yes-
terday. The final address was made
by the counsel for the defence and
of the accused themselves.

The legal proceedings yesterday
evening, with only a short adjourn-
ment. The verdict is expected to be
announced on April 26.

The court room was packed to
the roof with a large crowd com-
prising students, lawyers and in-
tellectuals.

The proceedings opened with a
brief address by the prosecutor,
who asked for the maximum sen-
tence for the accused on the ground
that they were guilty of crimes
against the State under Article 2
of the law governing emergency
measures for suppressing acts en-
dangering the National Govern-
ment. He further stated that the
evidence adduced proved that the
accused were members of an organ-
isation whose object was to over-
throw the National Government.

Chen Tu-hsiu then made a state-
ment in his own defence. He claimed
that he had never been a member
of the Communist Party since 1927,
and that he had only employed
words in opposing the Nanking Gov-
ernment. He further stated that he
had never advocated the overthrow
of the National Government by
force, but had only expressed his
opinions by means of articles pub-
lished in newspapers and magazines.

He claimed that the nation
had now reached a most critical
point of its history and that it
would be criminal for the people to
remain in the present state of af-
fairs. He claimed that he was act-
uated by patriotic motives that he
opposed the present "ruling class"
and that it was he and his col-
leagues, and not the present rulers,
who had really the interest of the
people at heart. In conclusion,
Chen contended that his opposition
to the Kuomintang and the
National Government was only
confined to words and thought and
that he had not yet so far taken
any active steps to overthrow the
existing regime. He demanded
therefore an acquittal, pointing out
that his actions were not criminal
under law.

Chen was followed by his co-ac-
cused, Mr. Chang Shih-chao, former
minister of justice under the Pei-
yang regime. Mr. Chang spoke elo-
quently on behalf, submitting exten-
sive juridical and political argu-
ments in defence of his client.

Chang Supports Action

He claimed that it was quite law-
ful for a party in opposition to cri-
ticise the Party in power, and the
Trotsky faction of which Chen was
the leader, had never taken up
arms against the National Gov-
ernment, and that they were only
expressing their opinions by means
of articles published in newspapers
and magazines. He further stated
that the actions of the accused were
not criminal under the existing laws
of the land.

He further maintained that the
defence had not yet reached the
stage of propaganda. Moreover, the
methods of the phrases advanced
by the accused and the Communists
were similar to those laid down by
the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen in his
Three People's Principles. He also
contended that the criticisms of
the Kuomintang made by his client
were fair and well-founded, and
that therefore his client ought to
be regarded not as an enemy, but
rather as a friend of the Kuo-
mintang.

Finally, the defence counsel re-
called the past cooperation between
his client and the Kuomintang. He
stated that at one time Chen served as
provincial commissioner of education
in Kwangtung under the Kuomin-
tang regime. In 1923, he went to
Russia in company with a Kuomin-
tang commissioner. In 1927, as
Leader of the Communist Party, he
issued with Mr. Wang Ching-wei a
joint manifesto supporting the then
political situation.

Mr. Chang concluded by demand-
ing the unconditional acquittal of
his client.

After a short adjournment the proceed-
ings were resumed. The political
arguments advanced by the
counsel for the defence were met
by the prosecutor, who contended
that the accused were guilty of
crimes against the State.

The prosecutor further stated
that the accused had attempted to
overthrow the National Government
by force, and that their actions
were criminal under the existing
laws of the land.

The prosecutor further maintained
that the accused were members of
an organisation whose object was
to overthrow the National Govern-
ment. He further stated that the
evidence adduced proved that the
accused were guilty of crimes
against the State under Article 2
of the law governing emergency
measures for suppressing acts en-
dangering the National Govern-
ment.

The prosecutor concluded by de-
manding the maximum sentence
for the accused.

Before the trial was concluded,
each of the accused was given an
opportunity of making his state-
ment. Several of them denied hav-
ing any connection with the Com-
munist Party, while others admitted
that they were members of the
Communist Party, but denied that
they had ever advocated the over-
throw of the National Government
by force.

（批：Reg. Please attach white. JHS APR. 22 1933）

陈独秀
审讯结束，
26日宣判

托派称其仅以言论
反对南京政府

称反对国民党并非
反对国家

南京，4月21日.—（路透社）—
中国共产党托洛茨基派领袖陈独秀及其他九名涉嫌共产党员的审判，昨日在江苏高等法院分院复庭。辩护律师及被告本人作了最后陈述。

昨日晚间的法律程序仅短暂休庭。预计将于4月26日宣布判决。

法庭内挤满了大量人群，包括学生、律师和知识分子，可谓座无虚席。

诉讼程序以检察官的简短陈述开始，他要求对被告判处最高刑罚，理由是被告犯有《危害民国紧急治罪法》第二条规定的危害国家罪。他进一步指出，所提出的证据证明被告是一个旨在推翻国民政府的组织的成员。

随后，陈独秀作了自我辩护陈述。他声称自1927年以来从未加入过共产党，并且他在反对南京政府时仅使用了言论手段。他进一步表示，他从未主张以武力推翻国民政府，而只是通过在报纸和杂志上发表文章来表达他的观点。

他声称，国家现在已处于历史上最危急的时刻，人民若维持现状将是犯罪之举。他声称，他反对当前的“统治阶级”是出于爱国动机，并且真正关心人民利益的是他和他的同事，而非当前的统治者。最后，陈独秀辩称，他对国民党和国民政府的反对仅限于言论和思想层面，他尚未采取任何积极步骤来推翻现有政权。因此，他要求宣告无罪，指出其行为在法律上不构成犯罪。

陈独秀之后是他的同案被告张士钊先生，他是北洋政府时期的前司法总长。张先生代表被告发表了雄辩的讲话，提出了广泛的法律和政治论点为其当事人辩护。

张支持该行动

他声称，反对党批评执政党是完全合法的，陈独秀作为领袖的托洛茨基派从未对国民政府拿起武器，他们只是通过在报纸和杂志上发表文章来表达观点。他进一步指出，根据现行国家法律，被告的行为不构成犯罪。

他进一步坚持认为，辩护方尚未达到宣传的阶段。此外，被告和共产党人提出的措辞方法与已故孙中山博士在其《三民主义》中规定的方法相似。他还辩称，其当事人对国民党的批评是公平且有根据的，因此其当事人不应被视为敌人，而应被视为国民党的朋友。

最后，辩护律师回顾了其当事人与国民党过去的合作。他指出，陈独秀曾在国民党执政时期担任广东省教育厅厅长。1923年，他与一名国民党委员一同前往俄国。1927年，作为共产党领袖，他与汪精卫先生联合发表宣言，支持当时的政治局势。

张先生最后要求无条件释放其当事人。

短暂休庭后，诉讼程序恢复。辩护律师提出的政治论点遭到检察官的反驳，检察官坚持认为被告犯有危害国家罪。

检察官进一步指出，被告企图以武力推翻国民政府，其行为根据现行国家法律构成犯罪。

检察官进一步坚持认为，被告是一个旨在推翻国民政府的组织的成员。他进一步指出，所提出的证据证明被告犯有《危害民国紧急治罪法》第二条规定的危害国家罪。

检察官最后要求对被告判处最高刑罚。

在审判结束前，每名被告都有机会发表陈述。其中几人否认与共产党有任何联系，而其他人承认他们是共产党成员，但否认曾主张以武力推翻国民政府。

（批注：登记。请附白色副本。JHS 1933年4月22日）

Afternoon Translation
COM. UNIST.
Sin Wan Pao: (Nanking Telegram):
THE TRIAL OF CHEN TOU SEU.
The trial of Chen Tou Seu was continued on the morning of April 20 at the Nanking District Court.
The procurator alleged that Chen had organized movements for the overthrow of the National Government and the Kuomintang and that he was a member of the Standing Committee of the Opposition Party of Communist Leftist Clique. On these grounds, he alleged that Chen had violated Articles 2 and 6 of the National Emergency Law. Feng Su Tze was declared by the Procurator to be equally guilty as Chen Tou Seu. As to Wang Mu and Pok Yi Fan, he submitted that although they were declared by Chen and Peng never to have been reserve members of the Standing Committee of the Communist Party, they had been identified by Hsia Hsao San so they had also violated Article 6 of the Emergency Law. The remaining accused, he contended, were like-wise guilty. In conclusion, he submitted that the present case was less grave than theoulens Case, therefore the punishment should be lighter than life imprisonment.
The lawyer for the first accused, Chen Tou Seu, argued that as the Court was not a court of the Kuomintang party only, all who are opposing the Kuomintang or the National Government should not be regarded as having committed any crime endangering the country. The phenomenon of a party not in power attacking the Government was common in politics in all countries. Political rivalry did not come within the jurisdiction of the law, and it would be most ridiculous if China were to impose punishment upon political opponents. The points brought out by the procurator can therefore not be established. According to Article 103 of the Criminal Law, those who oppose the Government in a lawful manner are not committing a crime. As to the propagating of Communism, the promotion of equal land rights etc. these matters have already been included in the doctrines of Sun Yat Sen. If Chen Tou Seu were to be punished because of this, then how about it fare with those who follow the principles of Sun Yat Sen? Furthermore, according to the three points in Chen Tou Seu's statement, his opposition to the Kuomintang was not based on Communism. His opposition to the Kuomintang was intended to reform and protect the Kuomintang. This is the kind of man the Kuomintang requires. Although Chen investigated Communism, he had no connection with any Communist party; he had no relations whatsoever with the Kiangsi and Hunan Communists or with the Third International; he had even no direct communication with the Trotsky Party. As to Feng Su Tze, he had frankly confessed that he was a Communist, but his opposition of the Government and the Kuomintang arose out of his patriotism. He did not propagate Communism.
As to Pok Yi Fan, the Communist books seized in his room belonged to a friend. He was not a reserve member of the Communist Standing Committee. Furthermore, according to Article 520 of the explanations of the Judicial Yuan, the keeping of Communist books did not constitute an offence. The others all pleaded that they had been compelled by hardship to print Communist literature.

共产主义者。
《新闻报》：（南京电报）：
陈独秀受审案。
陈独秀的审判于4月20日上午在南京地方法院继续进行。
检察官指控陈独秀组织旨在推翻国民政府和国民党的运动，并称其为共产党左倾反对派常设委员会成员。基于此，他指控陈独秀违反了《危害民国紧急治罪法》第二条和第六条。检察官宣布冯嗣同（音译）与陈独秀同样有罪。至于王幕（音译）和濮一凡（音译），他提出，虽然陈独秀和彭述之（音译）宣称他们从未担任共产党常设委员会候补委员，但夏少三（音译）已指认他们，因此他们也违反了《紧急治罪法》第六条。他主张其余被告同样有罪。最后，他提出本案情节较“牛兰案”为轻，因此刑罚应轻于无期徒刑。
第一被告陈独秀的律师辩称，既然法院并非仅为国民党设立的法庭，所有反对国民党或国民政府的人都不应被视为犯有危害国家罪。在野党攻击政府的现象在所有国家的政治中都很常见。政治斗争不属于法律管辖范围，如果中国惩罚政治对手，那将是最荒谬的。因此，检察官提出的要点不能成立。根据《刑法》第103条，以合法方式反对政府者不构成犯罪。至于传播共产主义、提倡平均地权等，这些内容已包含在孙中山的学说中。如果因此惩罚陈独秀，那么遵循孙中山原则的人又将如何？此外，根据陈独秀声明中的三点，他对国民党的反对并非基于共产主义。他反对国民党是为了改革和保护国民党。这正是国民党所需要的人才。虽然陈独秀研究过共产主义，但他与任何共产党都没有联系；他与江西和湖南的共产党人或第三国际没有任何关系；他甚至与托洛茨基派没有直接联系。至于冯嗣同，他坦率承认自己是共产党员，但他对政府和国民党的反对是出于爱国主义。他并未传播共产主义。
至于濮一凡，在他房间里搜获的共产主义书籍属于一位朋友。他不是共产党常设委员会的候补委员。此外，根据司法院解释第520条，持有共产主义书籍不构成犯罪。其他人均辩称，他们是因生活所迫才印刷共产主义文献。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, APRIL 16, 1933

Trial Of Reds
Is Opened At
Nanking Court

Chen Tu-hsiu, Comrades
Nabbed Here Come Up
Before High Tribunal

Prisoner Admits Link
With Communist Party

NANKING, April 14.—(Reuters).
—The trial of Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu
and ten other Communists opened
here at 10 o'clock this morning be-
fore Judge Hu Shan-ching, chief of
the criminal section of the Kiangsu
High Court, who was assisted by
two other judges.
Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu was the first
to be examined, the others being
removed from the court-room dur-
ing his questioning. Replying to all
questions with great ease and calm-
ness, Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu admitted his
connection with the Chinese Com-
munist Party, saying he had been
secretary-general of the Trotsky
group, but had afterwards been ex-
pelled from the party owing to
political differences.
Questioned concerning the activi-
ties of the Trotsky group in China.
Mr. Chen said that all the informa-
tion desired was contained in docu-
ments already in the court's posses-
sion and therefore requested the
judge not to put any further ques-
tions on the subject "in order to
save time."
The aim of the Trotsky group, he
said, was to relieve the masses
from their sufferings. He expressed
the opinion that there was no pos-
sibility of a compromise between the
Communists and capitalists. It was
understandable, he said, why the
Communist Party must possess mili-
tary force in order to achieve poli-
tical power, as the rise of the Kuo-
mintang had been preceded by
military campaigns.
Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu declared that
Pu Yi-fan, one of the eleven pri-
soners, was not the executive head
of the Trotsky group and had pro-
bably been arrested by mistake. The
real executive head of the Trotsky
group, he added, was a man
whose name he refused to give.
He also stated that he had no
knowledge of the whereabouts of
any other members of the group.
When asked if he had any con-
nection with the Soviet Govern-
ment, he replied in the negative.
He further stated that he had no
knowledge of any plans for an up-
rising in China.
The trial is expected to last sev-
eral days.

红色分子审判
在南京法院
开庭

陈独秀及其同志
在此被捕后出庭
受高等法庭审理

囚犯承认与共产党
有关联

南京，4月14日.—（路透社）.—
今天上午10时，陈独秀先生及其他十名共产党员的审判在此开庭，主审法官为江苏高等法院刑事庭庭长胡善敬（音译），另有两名法官协助审理。
陈独秀先生首先接受讯问，其他人在讯问期间被带离法庭。陈独秀先生轻松冷静地回答了所有问题，承认他与中国共产党有关联，称他曾担任托洛茨基派的总书记，但后来因政治分歧被开除出党。
当被问及托洛茨基派在中国的活动时，陈先生表示，所需的所有信息都包含在法院已掌握的文件中，因此请求法官不要再就此事提问，“以节省时间”。
他说，托洛茨基派的目标是减轻民众的痛苦。他表示，共产党人与资本家之间不可能妥协。他说，可以理解为什么共产党必须拥有军事力量才能获得政治权力，因为国民党的崛起也是 preceded by 军事战役。
陈独秀先生声明，十一名囚犯之一的濮一凡并非托洛茨基派的执行负责人，可能是被误捕。他补充说，托洛茨基派真正的执行负责人是一个他拒绝透露姓名的人。
他还表示，他不知道该派其他任何成员的下落。
当被问及是否与苏联政府有联系时，他予以否认。他进一步表示，他不知道中国有任何起义计划。
预计审判将持续数天。

January 9, 1933. Morning Translation.

COMMUNISM

Citizens Daily (市民报) of January 8:
PRECAUTIONS AGAINST COMMUNIST DISTURBANCES.
Owing to rumours that Communists will create disturbances, the French Police has increased the number of detectives and policemen patrolling Rue Brissonnet, Rue Ratard, Rue Brenier de Montmorand, Moulmein Road end, Changtu Road end and vicinity. Commencing from 5 p.m. each day, pedestrians are searched as a measure against untoward incidents.

Dah Kung Jih Pao (大公報), a mosquito paper, of January 8:
THE CHEN TOU-SEU CASE.
After having been sentenced to death by the Kiangsu High Court, Chen Tou-seu retained lawyer Tsang Sz-chuan to make an appeal to the Judicial Yuan. The Chief of the Yuan is at Geneva and the Deputy-Chief can not deal with the matter.
In a conversation with General Chiang Kai-shek, General Ho Ying-ching, Minister of War, stated that Chen had committed no great offences against the Kuomintang; that he had been beneficial to education in the May 4 Movement; that the organization of the Trotsky Clique was an anti-Communist move. He suggested that Chen be used against the Communist and he be granted a special amnesty.
This opinion was agreeable to General Chiang Kai-shek who then negotiated with Dr. Lo Wen-kan, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Chao Yuan-tsung, Acting President of the Legislative Yuan, which resulted in General Ho's suggestions being accepted.
The matter has been referred to the Canton authorities.

LABOUR

Chen Pao and other local newspapers:
TELEGRAPH MESSENGERS RESUME WORK.
With reference to the strike of messengers of the Great Northern, the Great Eastern and the Pacific Companies, direct negotiations with the management have opened by the strikers and as a result it was agreed that ten strikers of the three Companies be dismissed and the others be reinstated.
Work was resumed by the men on January 7.
The foreign boys who had been employed to undertake the delivery of telegrams were discharged and the wages for December of the ten dismissed men were issued by the managements.

共产主义

1月8日《市民报》：
防范共产党人骚乱之措施。
鉴于有谣言称共产党人将制造骚乱，法国警察增加了在布里索内路（Rue Brissonnet）、拉塔德路（Rue Ratard）、布雷尼埃·德·蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）、穆尔明路（Moulmein Road）尽头、昌图路（Changtu Road）尽头及附近地区巡逻的侦探和警员数量。自每日下午5时起，对行人进行搜查，以防不测事件发生。

1月8日的小报《大公報》：
陈独秀案。
陈独秀被江苏高等法院判处死刑后，聘请律师臧松泉向司法院提出上诉。该院院长目前在日内瓦，副院长无法处理此事。
军政部长何应钦将军在与蒋介石将军的谈话中表示，陈独秀并未对国民党犯下重大罪行；他在五四运动中对教育有益；托洛茨基派系的组织是一项反共举措。他建议利用陈独秀来对抗共产党，并予以特赦。
这一意见得到了蒋介石将军的认可，随后蒋与外交部长罗文干博士及立法院代理院长赵元宗进行协商，结果何应钦的建议被采纳。
此事已移交广东当局处理。

劳工

《申报》及其他本地报纸：
电报信差复工。
关于大北公司、大东公司和太平洋公司信差的罢工一事，罢工者已与资方展开直接谈判，结果是三家公司的十名罢工者被解雇，其余人员复职。
工人们于1月7日复工。
此前受雇投递电报的外国童工已被解雇，资方已发放被解雇的十人十二月份的工资。

Subject (in full) Memorandum on "The Trotsky Opposition Clique".

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by O.L.D. Sweeney

The arrest of Chen To Seu (陈独秀), leader of the
Trotsky Opposition Clique, by the Municipal Police in October
1932 dealt a blow to the anti-Stalin group of Communists in China which,
for the time being, has rendered its opposition practically
null and from which it may never recover.

As far back as 1926 Chen To Seu's lukewarm policy in
directing the movements of the Chinese Bolsheviks throughout
China by virtue of his position as head of the Executive
Committee of the Bolshevik Party in this country was costing
him a loss of prestige in Moscow. His popularity with the
Eastern Representatives of the IIIrd International steadily
waned and in 1927 he was summoned to present himself
in Moscow. On his disregarding the order he was expelled from
the Party. Since his expulsion Chen has consistently opposed
the IIIrd International and the Central Committee of the
Chinese Communist Party.

His attachment to the theories and practices of Trotskyism
may be dated from the time of his dismissal from the Party.

The distinction between the style of Communism as
practised by Chen To Seu and that at present in vogue in
Soviet Russia is a purely academic one.

This erstwhile comrade of Chiang Kai-shek was not in
favour of the sanguinary policy of communists and once
stigmatised the Red army as bandits. The policy of the
Stalinites to accomplish the Bolshevisation of the whole world
through the medium of propaganda inciting the proletarians to
rise and massacre all those set up in authority over them and
by insidious literature tending to promote internecine strife,
the fostering of strikes and other disorders which might assist

主题（全称） 关于“托洛茨基反对派系”的备忘录。

由 D.S. Jones 撰写，经 O.L.D. Sweeney 转呈

1932年10月，工部局警务处逮捕了托洛茨基反对派系领袖陈独秀（Chen To Seu），这对中国的反斯大林共产主义团体造成了打击，使其反对活动暂时实际上归于无效，且可能永远无法恢复元气。

早在1926年，陈独秀凭借其在华布尔什维克党执行委员会主席的地位，指导中国各地布尔什维克运动时采取的温和政策，导致他在莫斯科的声望受损。他在共产国际东方代表中的受欢迎程度 steadily waning（稳步下降），并于1927年被召往莫斯科。因他无视该命令，被开除出党。自被开除以来，陈一直反对共产国际和中国共产党中央委员会。

他对托洛茨基主义理论和实践的依附，可追溯至他被开除出党之时。

陈独秀所实行的共产主义风格与目前苏维埃俄罗斯流行的共产主义风格之间的区别，纯粹是学术性的。

这位蒋介石的前同志并不赞成共产党人的血腥政策，曾一度斥责红军为匪徒。斯大林派通过宣传煽动无产阶级起义并屠杀所有凌驾于他们之上的权威人物，以及通过旨在促进内部 strife（冲突）的阴险文献、助长罢工和其他有助于

在传播其理论时，托洛茨基反对派系采用了与斯大林集团大致相同的方法；分发共产主义文献、小册子等；举行秘密会议；在农民、工人和学生中进行宣传；通过付费代理人的诡计诱骗新成员加入等等。
与接受莫斯科大量补贴以资助事业的斯大林追随者不同，托洛茨基派系的资金几乎完全依赖于党员和外部同情者的自愿捐款。在后一类人中，可以列举以下国民党成员的名字——在当地政治中颇有名气的蔡元培博士、杨杏佛先生和周佛海先生。当然，由于没有数据表明任何一方的财务状况，我们可以相当有把握地假设，像拥有莫斯科政府支持的斯大林派系这样的组织，在财力上要比很大程度上依赖支持者慷慨解囊的托洛茨基反对派强大得多。
关于托洛茨基党总人数的数据不可得，该党的多数成员分布在相距甚远的地方，如华北（北平）和华南（福建）。然而据知，

Extract from Daily Intelligence Report of Feb. 20, 1932.

Association of War Suffering Schoolmates of
various universities.

Between 10.30 a.m. and 3 p.m. February 19, about
110 students of various local schools held a meeting in
the Young Men's Lecturing Group Society Building, Small
West Gate, to inaugurate a new organization entitled
"Association of War suffering schoolmates of various
Universities". Wong Ts Liang(王子良), a student of the
Vincent English School( No. 3 Lane 84, Medhurst Road), Chen
Sing Yih(陳心益) and Wong Tsai Zyan(王燦然), students of
the Chinese Public School at Woosung, presided. Discussion
on measures to relieve schoolmates now in distress as a result
result of the outbreak of hostilities between Japanese and
Chinese troops took place and the following resolutions were
passed:-

1) That all schoolmates in distress be instructed to proceed
to the University Students National Salvation Committee,
the temporary office of which is (according to the students)
in the Shanghai College of Law, 450 Rue Pere Robert, at 1 p.m.
February 20 to demand the handing over to this Committee
the fund formerly raised by public contributions for the
purposes of supporting the Volunteer Army in Manchuria.

3) That a circular appeal be sent to various places in
Kwantung requesting them to remit contributions to this
committee.

2) That the same demand be submitted to the Middle School
Students National Salvation Committee, 15 Chih Ping Li,
Chung Hwa Road.

4) That a manifesto be issued disclosing the atrocities of
the Japanese.

5) That ten open-air lecturing groups of three persons
each be organized to extend the Anti-Japanese propaganda.

6) That separate groups be also formed to solicit contributions
from local organizations to the fund for purchasing comforts
for soldiers.

7) That communications be established with various local
anti-Japanese organizations.

8) That a Committee of 13 members be appointed.

It is reported that the temporary correspondence
address of this organization is Hwa Tung Lodging House,
No. 54 Ching Yih Li(靜安里), Rue Brenier de Montmorand,

各大学战难同学联合会。

2月19日上午10时30分至下午3时之间，约110名本地各校学生在小西门青年宣讲团社大楼举行会议，成立一个名为“各大学战难同学联合会”的新组织。文氏英文学校（麦赫斯特路84弄3号）学生王子良（Wong Ts Liang）、吴淞中国公学学生陈心益（Chen Sing Yih）和王燦然（Wong Tsai Zyan）担任主席。会议讨论了救济因中日军队爆发敌对行动而陷入困境的同学的措施，并通过以下决议：-

1) 指示所有处于困境的同学于2月20日下午1时前往大学生救国会（据学生称，其临时办公室位于罗伯特神父路450号上海法学院），要求将该会以前为支援东北义勇军而公开募集的资金移交给该委员会。

3) 向广东各地发送通函呼吁，请求它们向该委员会汇款捐赠。

2) 向中华路志平里15号的中学生救国会提出同样的要求。

4) 发布宣言，揭露日本的暴行。

5) 组织十个露天宣讲组，每组三人，以扩展抗日宣传。

6) 另组建小组，向本地各机构募捐，用于购买慰问士兵的物品基金。

7) 与本地各抗日组织建立联系。

8) 任命一个由13名成员组成的委员会。

据报道，该组织的临时通信地址为布雷尼埃·德·蒙莫朗路静安里54号华东旅社，

During the autumn of 1931 it would appear that the person refer-
red to in the attached memo as Mr. Jeela may have resided in the
house in question prior to the autumn of 1931.
Mrs Borovsky and her sister were interviewed, but they were
unable to give the names of persons who had resided in their
house during 1930 and 1931. However, they are positive that no
one bearing the name of Mr. Jeela was among those persons. They
were all of Russian nationality, with the exception of a Chinese
who rented a room during the period May-July 1931 at a monthly
rate of $ 45.00. He was about 35-38 years of age, wore foreign
style clothes and conveyed the impression of being an educated
man. Apparently he was unemployed and stayed most of the time in
his room where he had a quantity of books, several Chinese males
visited him and he received a considerable number of letters.
Neither his name nor present address is known to Mrs Borovsky.
Inquiries made at the boarding-house section of the
French Police have proved abortive owing to the fact that the
house registers for 1930 and 1931 had already been destroyed.
G. Prokofieff

博罗夫斯基夫人及其妹妹接受了问询，但她们无法提供1930年和1931年期间居住在其房屋内的人员姓名。然而，她们确信这些人中没有名为吉拉先生的人。除了一名中国人在1931年5月至7月期间以每月45.00美元的价格租用了一个房间外，其他人均为俄罗斯国籍。这名中国人年龄约35-38岁，穿着西式服装，给人的印象是一位受过教育的人。他显然处于失业状态，大部分时间待在自己的房间里，房内有许多书籍，有几名中国男性曾拜访他，他也收到了大量信件。博罗夫斯基夫人既不知道他的姓名，也不知道他目前的地址。
向法国警察总局寄宿管理处进行的查询均无结果，因为1930年和1931年的房屋登记簿已被销毁。

With reference to the Officer i/c Special Branch
instructions of November 3 on the subject of telephone numbers
used by certain prisoners in the case against Chen Tou Seu et al,
in the presence of D.S. Moore, I have to report that diligent
inquiries to ascertain the identities of the persons telephoned
to have so far been without result.
(1) Telephone No.93440, used by Wong Siao Tsung (photo
B.9524), belongs to China News Service (Shanghai Branch),
Room 425 Continental Building, Nanking and Shantung Roads
corner.
(2) Telephone No. 91631, used by Wong Ts Bing (王子平)
alias Tsung Man (Photo B.9525), belongs to the Yuen Ming
Chemical Dyeing Company (元明 ), No.504/6 Tientsin Road.
In order to ascertain whether the prisoners were
known to the above mentioned concerns or any of their employees,
an agent, posing as a hotel servant was sent on November 9th and
10th to deliver two bogus letters addressed to the prisoners
c/o these concerns containing a pretext that the sender had
recently arrived in Shanghai and desired to meet them. The
inmates of the two concerns, upon seeing the names of the
envelopes, denied knowing anything about them or the whereabouts
of their relatives. The possibility of these denials was
foreseen for the inmates of the concerns in question were no
doubt aware of the arrest of Chen Tou Seu and his associates
and would naturally be afraid to admit knowing such persons
for fear of getting into trouble.

为了查明囚犯是否为上述机构或其任何员工所认识，一名特工伪装成旅馆侍者，于11月9日和10日投递了两封寄给囚犯并转交上述机构的假信，信中借口发件人最近抵达上海并希望与他们见面。这两家机构的内部人员在看到信封上的名字后，否认认识这些人或知道其亲属的下落。这种否认的可能性已在预料之中，因为相关机构的内部人员无疑知晓陈独秀及其同伙被捕一事，自然会因为害怕惹上麻烦而不敢承认认识这些人。

French Political Branch,
November 14, 1932

R.T 159/
Arrests of Chen Tu Hsiu in the French Concession

Chen Tu Hsiu (陳獨秀) alias Chen Ti Pu (陳迪甫), former
member of the Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party,
no leader of the Leftish opposition of the Party, was arrested
twice by the French Police.

1. On October 4, 1921 during a raid made at No.2, Passage 365,
Route Vallon, where the offices and booksellers' shop of the
revue "Youth" were installed. At that time this revue was the
official organ of the Chinese Communist Party. In 1920 the
bookshop of the "Youth" revue was situated in Rue du Consulat,
but it was closed by the French Police on February 4, 1921.
Among the documents seized at the home of Chen Tu Hsiu
was a letter addressed to him by Henri Barbusse, the well known
French radical writer.
sentenced
The French Mixed Court condemned Chen Tu Hsiu to a
fine of 100 dollars for infringement of Consular réglt No.5.

It should be noted that on March 16, 1921 General Tch'ng
Ki, Military Governor of Canton, sent a letter to Mr De la
Prade, Consul-General of France at Shanghai, requesting him to
return to Chen Tu Hsiu the books seized by the French Police on
Feb.4, 19 32 (?) during the first raid made on the booksellers
for the "Youth" revue which, "could not be considered as dangerous
from the viewpoint of the propagation of anarchist and Bolchevist
principles."

2. In 1922 Chen Tu Hsiu installed himself once more in the French
Concession, continuing to spread communist ideas in China. The
French Police arrested him for the second time in April 1922. On
April 18 he was arraigned before the French Mixed Court and
fined 400 dollars for infringement of Article 221 of the Chinese
Criminal Code and Consular Order No.5.

(signed) Emelianoff

法国政治处，
1932年11月14日

R.T 159/
法租界逮捕陈独秀案

陈独秀（Chen Tu Hsiu），别名陈迪甫（Chen Ti Pu），前中国共产党中央委员会委员，党内左翼反对派领袖，曾被法国警察逮捕两次。

1. 1921年10月4日，在搜查瓦隆路365弄2号时被捕，当时《青年》杂志的办事处和书店设于此地。当时该杂志是中国共产党的官方机关刊物。1920年，《青年》杂志的书店位于领事馆路，但于1921年2月4日被法国警察关闭。
在陈独秀家中查获的文件中，有一封法国著名激进作家亨利·巴比塞（Henri Barbusse）写给他的信。
判决
法国会审公廨判处陈独秀罚款100美元，罪名是违反领事规章第5号。

值得注意的是，1921年3月16日，广东督军陈炯明将军致函法国驻上海总领事德拉普拉德先生（Mr De la Prade），请求他将法国警察在1932年2月4日（原文如此，疑为1921年）第一次搜查《青年》杂志书店时没收的书籍归还给陈独秀，理由是这些书籍“从传播无政府主义和布尔什维克原则的角度来看，不能被视为危险物品。”

2. 1922年，陈独秀再次定居法租界，继续在中国传播共产主义思想。法国警察于1922年4月第二次逮捕了他。4月18日，他被提审至法国会审公廨，因违反《中华民国刑法》第221条和领事命令第5号，被罚款400美元。

（签名） Emelianoff

actuellement leader de l'opposition de gauche du parti, a été

1921.
Parmi les documents saisis chez CHEN TU HSIU, se trouvait

La Cour Mixte Française a condamné CHEN TU HSIU à 100 dol-

A noter que le 16 Mars 1921, le général TCHANGKI, gouverneur

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 10, 1932

DEATH PENALTY FOR
CHEN URGED

Canton Kuomintang Says
He Was Behind All
Red Disorders

CANTON, Nov. 6.—It is reported that the Canton District Kuomintang has telegraphed to the Central Kuomintang in Nanking, requesting the execution of Chen Tu-hsiu, alleged Communist leader now held in custody at Nanking.

The telegram says that when he was in Canton he preached the “pernicious doctrine” of Communism to the public, thereby bringing about the Red rising of December, 1927, in which thousands of people were killed. It declares that Chen is responsible for all the Communist troubles of China in recent years, adding that if the authorities show a little delay in meting out the death penalty to him, the meaning of the party purification movement of 1928 as well as the present anti-Communist campaign will be entirely lost.

The Canton Kuomintang also charges Mr. Tsai Yuan-pei, Chairman of the National Research Academy with shielding Chen and suggests that a warning be addressed to him.

《字林西报》，1932年11月10日，星期四

要求对陈
处以死刑

广东国民党称
他是所有赤色
动乱的幕后主使

广州，11月6日电。——据报道，广东区国民党已致电南京国民党中央，请求处决目前被拘押在南京的所谓共产党领袖陈独秀。

电文称，他在广州期间向公众宣扬共产主义这一“有害学说”，从而导致了1927年12月的赤色起义，那次起义中数千人丧生。电文宣称，陈独秀应对近年来中国所有的共产主义麻烦负责，并补充说，如果当局在对他执行死刑方面稍有拖延，那么1928年党内清洗运动以及当前反共运动的意义将完全丧失。

广东国民党还指控国立研究院院长蔡元培先生庇护陈独秀，并建议向他发出警告。

November 6, 1932.
Morning Translation.

COMMUNISM

Min Pao and other local newspapers:

PRECAUTIONS ON SOVIET ANNIVERSARY, NOVEMBER 7.

November 7 being the 15th Anniversary of the Soviet Revolution in 1917 as well as the 1st Anniversary of the Establishment of the Central Provisional Government of Chinese Soviet Republic (1931), the Police authorities of Chinese controlled territory and of the foreign Settlement will declare special martial law in the districts under their respective jurisdiction with a view to guarding against possible disturbances by the Communists. Joint precautionary measures have been arranged by the Public Safety Bureau, the S.M.P. and the F.M.P. All meetings, processions, etc. will be prohibited on that day. Besides detailing additional policemen for duty, the Public Safety Bureau will dispatch detectives to patrol the streets and to search suspicious-looking persons.
Strict precautionary measures will be adopted by the S.M.P. in the eastern district where numerous factories and mills are located.

Sin Wan Pao:

Communistic Slogans and Red Flags on Electric Poles.

At 5 a.m. yesterday, policemen of the Patrol Corps of the 4th District Chinese Police Station, Chapel, noticed several electric poles on Chico Tang Road inscribed with Communistic slogans and affixed with red flags bearing on the words "Hasten a general strike."

China Times publishes the following telegram from Nanking:

THE NOULENS COUPLE.

The Ministry of Justice has not received an appeal from the Noulens couple demanding that they be allowed to live together and that they be removed to Soochow to serve their sentence. Information from the Ministry shows that the demand will not be accepted should it be submitted.

Sin Wan Pao:

THE KUOMINTANG REWARD OF $30,000.

Some time ago, the Central Kuomintang Headquarters offered a reward of $30,000 for information leading to the arrest of Chen Tou-seu, a notorious leader of the Communist Party. Chen has now been arrested by the Public Safety Bureau and sent to Nanking.
It is reported that the Central Kuomintang has commended the officers of the Public Safety Bureau for meritorious services in effecting the apprehension of Chen Tou-seu.

Reg. Please attach While
8/11/32

晨间译文。

共产主义

《民报》及其他本地报纸：

苏维埃纪念日（11月7日）的预防措施。

11月7日是1917年苏维埃革命15周年纪念日，也是中华苏维埃共和国中央临时政府成立（1931年）1周年纪念日，华界及外国租界的警察当局将在各自管辖区域内宣布特别戒严，以防范共产党人可能制造的骚乱。公安局、工部局警务处（S.M.P.）和公董局警务处（F.M.P.）已安排联合预防措施。当天禁止一切集会、游行等。除了增派警员执勤外，公安局还将派遣侦探巡逻街道并搜查形迹可疑之人。
工部局警务处将在工厂和纱厂众多的东区采取严格的预防措施。

《新晚报》：

电线杆上的共产主义标语和红旗。

昨日凌晨5时，第四区华捕巡捕房的巡捕在芝罘塘路（Chico Tang Road，音译）注意到几根电线杆上写有共产主义标语，并贴有写着“加速总罢工”字样的红旗。

《时报》刊登了如下来自南京的电讯：

努兰斯夫妇案。

司法部未收到努兰斯夫妇要求允许他们共同生活并将其移至苏州服刑的上诉。司法部的消息显示，即使提交该要求，也不会被接受。

《新晚报》：

国民党悬赏三万元。

此前，国民党中央总部悬赏三万元，征集线索以逮捕臭名昭著的共产党领袖陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu）。陈现已由公安局逮捕并送往南京。
据报道，国民党中央已表彰公安局官员在逮捕陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu）一案中的功绩。

in the compound of Central Station at 8 a.m. November 2, 1932.

LETTER TO SOLDIERS, CHINESE POLICEMEN AND POLICE CONSTABLE
BROTHERS ON THE ARREST OF CHEN TOU SEU, LEADER OF THE
ELIMINATION CLIQUE.

Dear brethren,

Chen Tou Seu, leader of the Anti-Revolutionary
Elimination Clique, and others were arrested by the Kuomintang
on October 16.

The members of the Elimination Clique are the running
dogs of the capitalistic classes. They say, "Under the
Kuomintang rule, labourers should not go on strike, but should
assist the capitalists to increase products. Labour strikes
will not bring victories. Peasants should not demand division
of land". Furthermore, they assist the Kuomintang in the
arrest of Communists, destruction of labour strikes,
denunciation of the Soviet Red Armies as bandits and act as
anti-revolutionary vanguards. But how is it that the
Kuomintang wishes to arrest them?

Brethren, you must know that the revolutionary
force of labourers and peasants is developing day by day and
that the Red Armies are constantly scoring victories. All the
labourers, peasants and poor people are aware that only the
Chinese Communist Party is working for their welfare and for
the emancipation of the Chinese race and that the Elimination
Cliques is treacherous. In face of the opposition, the
Elimination Clique discussed the situation with the Kuomintang
and the arrest of Chen Tou Seu was intended to make the people
believe that the Elimination Clique is revolutionary. At the
same time it fabricates rumours stating that Chen Tou Seu was
arrested on the information of the Chinese Communist Party.
These are the intrigues of the Kuomintang and the Elimination
Clique.

Brethren, we must unite under the leadership
of the Chinese Communist Party.

1932年11月2日上午8时，在中央车站大院邮件架中发现的一张传单的摘要译文。

致士兵、中国警察和巡捕兄弟书
关于逮捕“取消派”领袖陈独秀。

亲爱的兄弟们，

“反革命取消派”领袖陈独秀及其他人于10月16日被国民党逮捕。

取消派成员是资产阶级的走狗。他们说，“在国民党统治下，工人不应罢工，而应协助资本家增加产品。劳工罢工不会带来胜利。农民不应要求分地”。此外，他们协助国民党逮捕共产党人，破坏劳工罢工，诬蔑苏维埃红军为匪徒，并充当反革命先锋。但是，国民党为何又要逮捕他们呢？

兄弟们，你们必须知道，工农的革命力量日益发展，红军不断取得胜利。所有工人、农民和穷人都意识到，只有中国共产党在为他们的福利和中华民族的解放而奋斗，而取消派则是奸诈的。面对反对声，取消派与国民党商议局势，逮捕陈独秀意在让民众相信取消派是革命的。同时，他们捏造谣言，称陈独秀是根据中国共产党的情报被捕的。这些都是国民党和取消派的阴谋诡计。

兄弟们，我们必须在中国共产党的领导下团结起来。

November 2, 1932.

Enquiries made at Lunghwa Military Headquarters regarding
two prisoners released as referred to attached

Enquiries made at the Soong Wo Military Headquarters,
Lunghwa with reference to the release of two prisoners who
were handed over to them on May 25, 1931, and who were re-
arrested in the Settlement on October 15, the following has
been ascertained:-

1) Pan Yih Van (潘一凡) who gave his name as Tsu Teh King
(朱德明) when brought before the Military Court in May
1931, was sentenced to 2 years and 6 months imprisonment
for being in possession of communist literature. He was
subsequently transferred to Zau Oo Ching Gaol to serve his
sentence. At this time the Judge was not aware that he
was an important member of the Communist Party. Owing to
serious illness, the prisoner was released in February
1932 with the permission of the Head Gaoler.

2) Wong Woo (王武) who was then known as Liu Mow King
(刘梦庚) was sentenced by the Military Court, Lunghwa,
to five years imprisonment for a similar offence. He was
released on October 8, 1932, on the recommendation of Chen
Li Fu (陈立夫), member of the C.E.C. of Nationalist
Government in accordance with the Amnesty Act.

Remarks: "Commissioner of Police,
Sir,
Information. These men were re-arrested
in connection with the Chen To Seu Case, and have
again been handed over to the Chinese Authorities."

CHEN TU-SHIU
(China Critic)

Chen Tu-shiu, the well-known communist leader of the "Trotsky faction," was arrested on the 17th, together with eleven others of his associates. Since then, he has been transferred to Nanking under heavy guard, and it is reported that his request for a personal interview with General Chiang has been granted. It is not yet possible in no great detail, ... headed by Dr. Tsi Tsen-pai, Liu Ya-tse and others ... statement ... tion of his past services to the cause of the revolution ... of the constitution ... Mr. Chen was once editor of the revolutionary paper, Hsin Ching Nien, with Chien Hsuan-tung and Chang Shih-chao. He also served ... in the ... of the ... movement. ... at the Peking University ... age of the ... leaders of the May 4th Revolution ... Mr. Chen will be closely associated ... in the ... movement ... He was ... member ... and Liu Wen-tsai. The success of the movement was in a large measure due to the efforts put in by Chen Tu-shiu during this period, and ... from the movement itself and ... and Dr. Hu Shih. There are at present two factions in the Chinese Communist Party, one led by Chen Tu-shiu and the other by Li Li-san. While the latter advocates the policy of armed uprising and the establishment of Soviet governments in the rural districts, the former holds that the time is not yet ripe for such a policy and that the party should confine its activities to propaganda work among the workers and peasants. It is said that Chen Tu-shiu has been expelled from the party because of his opposition to the policy of Li Li-san. He is now living in Shanghai and is engaged in writing articles for various journals. His latest article, which appeared in a recent issue of the "China Critic," deals with the question of the relation between the Chinese Communist Party and the Third International. In this article he argues that the Chinese Communist Party should not be too closely tied up with the Third International, but should rather follow its own line of policy according to the actual conditions in China. He also criticises the policy of Li Li-san as being too radical and likely to lead to disaster. ...
