The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, October 29, 1932

Mme. Sun Protests
To the Editor:
I am astounded that all those who have come to the defense of Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu, far from protesting on the grounds of general political terror exercised by the Nanking Government, have not even said a word about the eleven men arrested with him.

Those who have come to the defense of Mr. Chen, his Chinese friends, and such organs as the Shanghai Times, the Journal de Changhai, and the China Critic, have done so largely on the grounds that Mr. Chen has disassociated himself from the revolutionary movement and because, according to these papers, he has called the Communist "bandits." That is no reason for me to come to his defense. Quite to the contrary. However, I protest against the arrest of Mr. Chen and his eleven colleagues, only because these arrests are another manifestation of the Terror, which the Kuomintang wages unceasingly against the Chinese working class, the peasants, and against student and revolutionary intellectuals, and occasionally against fractions within or close to the Kuomintang which even enjoy the support of some of its most influential members—as appears to be the case with Mr. Chen Tu-hsiu.

As an example of the fact that the present defenders of Chen Tu-hsiu are attempting to avoid the basic issue of political terror, we have the statements of individuals like Mr. Kwei Chung-shu who sought to give the impression in a recent article that these liberal Chinese and foreigners who came to the defense of Paul and Gertrude Ruegg did so only because they were foreigners and not because their arrest and persecution involved fundamental political issues, both national and international. They don't even point out now that among the thousands who fell before this terror, were two sons of Chen Tu-hsiu himself who were members of the Chinese Communist Party. Mr. Kwei sneeringly asked if Mr. Chen, like the Rueggs, had any children over whom sympathy could be aroused. Yes, he had two sons, both educated abroad, both labor organizers and one of them a poet of power and promise. They were shot to death by Chiang Kai-shek in 1927.

Men like Mr. Kwei and his fellow intellectuals remained silent then, and have remained silent through those ghastly years of the Terror against the Chinese people. But foreign workers of every land have not remained silent. In huge demonstrations and in their press everywhere, they have repeatedly denounced the Kuomintang terror and declared their solidarity with the cause and aspirations of the Chinese workers and peasants. They have raised money and formed committees, not only for the Rueggs, but for the past six years, for their tens of thousands of Chinese brothers. The hard-earned pennies of foreign workers have meant food and clothing for Chinese prisoners in Kuomintang prisons. Have Mr. Kwei and his like ever given a fraction as much? Hardly—and they are now trying to skirt the whole, fundamental issue of the Terror in China.

Against this Terror we need to wage an uncompromising struggle, and to make a start toward organizing this struggle I am ready to participate in the formation of a general committee in defense of all political prisoners, all victims of the Terror, and to such a movement I am ready to lend all my efforts and all my energies. I invite all the intellectuals of China, all friends of the Chinese people, to associate themselves with this Committee in a struggle against all political persecution.
SOONG CHING LING.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1932年10月29日，星期六

孙夫人抗议
致编辑：
令我震惊的是，所有那些为陈独秀先生辩护的人，非但没有就南京政府实施的一般性政治恐怖提出抗议，甚至对与他一同被捕的十一人只字未提。

那些为陈先生辩护的人，包括他的中国朋友，以及《上海泰晤士报》、《上海日报》和《中国评论》等机构，这样做的主要理由是陈先生已与革命运动划清界限，并且据这些报纸称，他曾称共产党人为“匪徒”。这并非我为他辩护的理由。恰恰相反。然而，我抗议逮捕陈先生及其十一位同事，仅因为这些逮捕是国民党对中国工人阶级、农民、学生和革命知识分子，以及偶尔对国民党内或其附近享有某些最具影响力成员支持的派系（陈独秀先生的情况似乎正是如此）不断发动的恐怖的另一种表现。

作为陈独秀目前的辩护者试图回避政治恐怖这一基本问题的例证，我们有像桂中枢先生这样的人的言论，他在一篇最近的文章中试图给人留下这样的印象：那些为 Paul 和 Gertrude Ruegg 辩护的自由派中国人和外国人之所以这样做，仅仅因为他们是外国人，而不是因为他们的逮捕和迫害涉及根本性的国内和国际政治问题。他们现在甚至没有指出，在这场恐怖中倒下的数千人中，包括陈独秀自己的两个儿子，他们都是中国共产党党员。桂先生讥讽地问，陈先生是否像 Ruegg 夫妇一样，有任何能激起同情的孩子。是的，他有两个儿子，都受过海外教育，都是劳工组织者，其中一位是有实力和前途的诗人。他们于1927年被蒋介石枪杀。

像桂先生及其同类知识分子那样的人当时保持沉默，并在针对中国人民的恐怖的那些可怕岁月里一直保持着沉默。但各国的外国工人并没有保持沉默。在大规模的示威活动中以及在各地的报刊上，他们一再谴责国民党的恐怖，并宣布他们与中国工人和农民的事业及愿望团结一致。他们筹集资金并成立委员会，不仅是为了 Ruegg 夫妇，而且在过去的六年里，是为了他们的成千上万的中国兄弟。外国工人辛苦挣来的便士意味着国民党监狱中中国囚犯的食物和衣物。桂先生及其同类是否曾给予过哪怕是一小部分？几乎没有——而他们现在正试图避开中国恐怖主义这一整个根本性问题。

为了对抗这种恐怖，我们需要开展毫不妥协的斗争，为了开始组织这场斗争，我准备参与组建一个保卫所有政治犯、所有恐怖受害者的总委员会，对于这样的运动，我准备贡献我所有的努力和精力。我邀请中国所有的知识分子、所有中国人民的朋友加入这个委员会，共同反对一切政治迫害。
宋庆龄。

Newspaper Translation dated October 29, 1932.

Sin Wan Poo.

CHEN TCU SEU'S ALLEGATION AGAINST S.M.P.

According to a Nanking telegram, Chen
Tou Seu is reported to have stated, while in the Nanking
Detention House, that the treatment he received at the hands
of the Shanghai Settlement Police was very bad.
We made inquiries of the Police and learned
that as Chen was indisposed, he was sent to hospital after
his arrest and had not been detained in any Station.
The allegation made by Chen was thus unfounded.
page_data.zh:
报纸译文，日期 1932年10月29日。

《新闻报》。

陈独秀对上海公共租界工部局警务处的指控。

据南京电报称，据报道 Chen Tou Seu 在南京拘留所期间表示，他在上海租界警察手中受到的待遇非常糟糕。
我们向警方查询后得知，由于陈身体不适，他在被捕后被送往医院，并未被拘押在任何巡捕房。
因此，陈的指控毫无根据。

Special Branch S.2. Station,
Date October 27. 19 32.
Subject (in full) Enquiry regarding Mr.T.F. Wei.
Made by D.S.I. Everest. Forwarded by
With reference to the attached "secret" enquiry from
the Officer i/c Special Branch regarding Mr.T.F. Wei, I have
to report having received the following information concerning
this individual from Mr.J.F. Rhame, General Manager of the
China Electric Co., Ltd:
T.F. Wei, native of Canton, left Canton for the
United States about the year 1914. He graduated from the
Boston Institute of Technology as a naval architect in 1919
and for the next year served in this capacity at the Newport
Dockyard. Returning to Canton in 1921 he took over an
official appointment in the Chinese Navy where he remained
until 1923. His movements during the next few years are
not known but in 1927 he was appointed managing director of
the Canton Arsenal. Towards the end of 1927, by reason of
certain political changes, he left this post and joined the
China Electric Co., Ltd., (Canton) as constructional engineer.
In 1929 he was transferred by this company to Shanghai and
remained in the same position until the autumn of 1930 when
he joined the Shanghai Telephone Co. Resigning from the
latter company in February 1932 he took over his present
position as general manager of the Chinese Telephone
Administration.
He is said to be the brother-in-law of the present
Minister of Railways, Mr. Koo Mung Yui (顧孟餘).
D. S. I.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

October 26, 1932. Morning Translation.

COMMUNIST.

Shun Pao (Nanking telegram):

THE CASE OF CHEN TOU SEU.

As a result of an investigation conducted by the highest military organ, Chen Tou Seu and Peng Su Tze will not be tried by a military court and the military will not interfere. The Chen Tou Seu case is similar to the Noulens case and the procedure in Chen's case will follow that in the Noulens case.

Callers On Chen Tou Seu Turned Away.

A certain girl named Wang Chek Yia, claiming to belong to Chen's family, demanded to visit Chen. She was accompanied by an official of the National Government. They were denied an interview with Chen, but permitted to write a note telling Chen that she had called. Chen has now slightly recovered from his stomach trouble.

-Kuo Min News Agency:-

Chen Tou Seu May Not Suffer Extreme Penalty.

After the extradition to Nanking of Chen Tou Seu, prominent local scholars including Tsai Yuan Pei, Lieu Yia Tze, Yang Hsin Foh and others appealed to the Central Government for leniency for Chen. Recently, General Chiang Kai Shek expressed the view that Chen will be transferred to the judicial authorities for trial and that all telegrams of appeal will be ignored.

According to Lo Wen Kan, the Foreign Minister, there is one thing in Chen Tou Seu's favour because he was expelled by the Communist Party. He may escape the extreme penalty.

Hu Shih Chih, the well known scholar, has also sent a telegram requesting Chen's release. Prominent lawyers in Peiping and Shanghai have requested Chen's transfer to the Judicial authorities.

Chen is now still detained in a military institution at Nanking. The decision of the military authorities to organize a Special Tribunal has now been abandoned. Trial by a Special Tribunal is not open to public and the sentence passed, is not published. This means that an accused may be executed after his crime has been proved. As Chen's principles are not harmful to society, he is exempt from trial by a Special Tribunal. Chen is suffering from Appendicitis and is under the care of the doctors of the Nanking Central Hospital.

S. 2
1932年10月26日。晨间译文。

共产党。

《申报》（南京电）：

陈独秀案。

经最高军事机关调查，陈独秀与彭述之将不由军事法庭审判，军方亦不干涉。陈独秀案类似牛兰案，陈案的处理程序将遵循牛兰案的先例。

探访陈独秀者被拒。

一名自称属于陈家亲属、名为王哲亚的女子要求探视陈独秀。她由一名国民政府官员陪同。他们被拒绝与陈独秀会面，但获准写一张便条告知陈独秀她曾来访。陈独秀目前的胃病已略有好转。

- 国民通讯社：-

陈独秀或可免遭极刑。

陈独秀被引渡至南京后，蔡元培、柳亚子、杨杏佛等当地知名学者向中央政府呼吁对陈从宽处理。近日，蒋介石将军表示，陈将被移交给司法机关受审，所有求情电报均将被忽略。

据外交部长罗文干称，陈独秀有一项有利因素，即他已被共产党开除。他或许能逃脱极刑。

著名学者胡适之也发电报请求释放陈独秀。北平和上海的知名律师请求将陈移交给司法机关。

陈目前仍被拘押在南京的一处军事机构中。军事当局组织特别法庭的决定现已放弃。特别法庭的审判不公开，判决也不公布。这意味着被告一旦罪行证实，即可能被处决。由于陈的主张对社会无害，故免除其由特别法庭审判。陈患有阑尾炎，正接受南京中央医院医生的护理。

Extract of Morning Translation dated 24/10/32

COMMUNISM.

Shun Pao (Nanking telegram):

THE ARREST OF CHEN TOU SEU.

Chen Tou Seu and Peng Su Tze are now being
detained in the Military Court. They are demanding to
see Kuo Lien Fu, Minister of Railways, and Chen Kung
Pok, Minister of Industries. Whether or not they will
be permitted to see the Ministers, it is not known.
The two ministers are absent from the capital.
The prisoners demanded to be provided with
newspapers and to write letters were rejected but they
were permitted to read Kuomintang books like the Three
Principles of the People etc. No callers are permitted.

Tsai Yuan Pei and Others Solicit Release of Chen Tou Seu.

Tsai Yuan Pei, Yang Hsin Fu, Liu Yia Tse, Ling
Yu Tang and other leading scholars in Shanghai yesterday
dispatched the following joint telegram to the National
Government and the Nanking Central Kuomintang Head-
quarters:-
"We are deeply concerned over the arrest and
extradition of Chen Tou Seu at a time when he is seriously
sick. In his early years, Chen Tou Seu was a well known
revolutionist against the Manchu regime and he was once
associated with Chang Pu Chuen and Tsang Hsin Yien, who
established the Kuo Min Jih Jih Pao Newspaper in Shanghai.
After the restoration movement, he assisted Peh Yun Ei
in governing Anhui Province with great merit. During
the May 4 movement, he indirectly helped the National
revolution. These meritorious acts should not be
disregarded. Later, he had a political difference
with the Kuomintang and joined the Communists, but it
must be recalled that he is opposed to the "rioting policy"
of the Communists and had condemned the "red army" as
bandits. For this attitude he was expelled by the
Communist Party some time ago. In European or American
Constitutional Governments, Chen Tou Seu would be regarded
simply as a member of the Communist Party in Congress.
We request that he be pardoned and saved from severe
punishment in order to give him a chance to repent".

1932年10月24日晨间翻译摘要

共产主义。

《申报》（南京电）：

陈独秀被捕。

陈独秀与彭述之现被羁押于军事法庭。他们要求会见铁道部长顾连福（音译）和工业部长陈公博。是否允许他们会见部长，尚不清楚。两位部长均不在首都。
囚犯要求提供报纸和写信的请求被驳回，但允许他们阅读《三民主义》等国民党书籍。禁止访客探视。

蔡元培等人请求释放陈独秀。

蔡元培、杨杏佛、刘亚子、林语堂及上海其他知名学者昨日向国民政府及南京国民党中央总部发出联合电报如下：
“我们对陈独秀在病重之际被捕并遭引渡深感关切。陈独秀早年曾是反对满清政权的著名革命家，曾与张溥泉（音译）及臧新燕（音译）交往，后者在上海创办了《国民日日日报》。复辟运动后，他协助柏云埃（音译）治理安徽省，功绩卓著。五四运动期间，他间接帮助了国民革命。这些功绩不应被忽视。后来，他与国民党产生政治分歧并加入共产党，但必须指出，他反对共产党的‘暴动政策’，并谴责‘红军’为匪徒。因此种态度，他不久前已被共产党开除。在欧美宪政政府中，陈独秀仅会被视为国会中的共产党员。我们请求予以宽恕，免除严惩，以给他悔过自新的机会”。

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, October 21, 1932

AS A CHINESE SEES IT

THE CASE OF CHEN TU-SHIU
By KWEI CHUNGSHU

LIKE the Noulens, Mr. Chen Tu-shiu, the famous communist leader, was arrested by the International Settlement police, expatriated by the Shanghai Special District Court and transferred to Nanking for trial on a charge of subversive activities against the government. If press reports are correct, he is being escorted to Hankow for an interview with General Chiang Kai-shek. Mr. Chen will probably admit that he is a communist. He may deep in his heart be proud of being a communist. And one may safely assume that he will face the trial like a true communist.

Mr. Chen claims to be a follower of Trotsky, and I was informed that he had taken the pains to explain to the judge who sat at the first hearing here the difference between his type of communism and that now in vogue in Soviet Russia. But the distinction is only academic. In the eyes of the law one communist is just as heir to punishment as another. No matter how much one may enjoy the study of communism as a doctrine, its militant tendency against constituted authority and order will ever be condemned by a society which frankly styles itself as capitalistic.

There is no intention on my part to defend Mr. Chen in any shape or manner. If the evidence adduced to have been seized by the police were found to be genuine, he would in due course receive appropriate sentence for espousing a cause which is at variance with the present social order.

Man Of Ideals

IT would be difficult, of course, to reconcile the advocacy of democratic principles in a republic with the suppression of thoughts and ideals. And Mr Chen, it would seem to the public, is a man of ideals and of devotion to them. But any one who pleads for the rule of law cannot permit sentiment to interfere with the course of justice. That justice may or may not be an approximation of the ideal being sought by jurists the world over, but unless substituted for by something better it has to remain the criterion of our daily conduct.

It was for this reason that the disinterested section of the public upheld the action of the Chinese judiciary in the Noulens' case. It will be for the same reason that the trial of Mr. Chen will be watched closely. It shows neither personal animosity toward him nor unconditional agreement with the policy of the government. It merely recognizes in the administration of the law as now existing.

Another Outrage

WHATEVER may be the result of Mr. Chen's trial, it is not permissible to discuss sub judice. One only wonders what has happened to the world's intellectuals and China's liberal champions who so vociferously defended the Noulens and equally vociferously denounced the present government.

Surely it would be outrageous to suggest that the intellectual lights espoused an international movement for the release of the Noulens for any other motives than that inspired by humanitarianism and human rights. They could have entertained no personal interest in the "victims" save for the cause they represented.

Now that Mr. Chen has found himself in the same plight as the Noulens, not a single voice has been raised on his behalf. If the Noulens were worthy of world-wide attention, Mr. Chen should be no less so, perhaps even more to the Chinese.

As a great Chinese scholar and one of the revolutionary leaders this country has ever had, he is certainly more deserving of the sympathy of Chinese liberals if any communist is so deserving. The only person who has shown any interest at all, strange to say, is General Chiang Kai-shek who has consented to grant the prisoner and erstwhile comrade a good hearing.

I am not pleading that the nation should rise and protest for Mr. Chen's sake. I did not so plead for the Noulens and I will not for him. But I do question why the self-same people who turned heaven and earth for the lives of the foreign communists should now display such appalling apathy toward the Chinese communist who once served China well.

Chen Is Suffering

MR. Chen is reported to be ill and suffering from insufficient clothing. The authorities were good enough to correct this inadequacy, but the standard bearers of humanity have not seized this point, as they did the alleged mistreatment of the Noulens, to broadcast heart-rending sob stories for him and against the government.

I do not know if Mr. Chen has a child as the Noulens have. If he does, the public has not been made aware of it, probably through the oversight of the dormant champions of human liberty. This human-interest phase of the case is well worth looking into, and I am passing this suggestion free to whomsoever it may concern.

The difference between the public reactions in two cases of an identical character is not incidental but deliberate. The victims are foreigners while Mr. Chen is not. What the Chinese government may do to a foreigner is a grave matter; what it does to a Chinese is immaterial. This is degrading to the foreigners but injurious to the Chinese. If this attitude is displayed by the man in the street, it is not quite serious. When it is shown by the self-styled liberal thinkers of the country, it is time for all of us to do a little reflective thinking.

But Mr. Chen's intellectual state is not swayed by their action or inaction.

（批：oic 8/3）

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1932年10月21日，星期五

中国人眼中的看法

陈独秀案
作者：桂中枢（KWEI CHUNGSHU）

与诺伦斯夫妇一样，著名共产党领袖陈独秀先生被公共租界警察逮捕，由上海特区法院驱逐出境，并以从事颠覆政府活动的罪名移交南京受审。如果新闻报道属实，他正被护送至汉口，以便与蒋介石将军会面。陈先生可能会承认自己是共产党员。他内心深处或许以身为共产党员为荣。我们可以稳妥地假设，他将像一名真正的共产党员那样面对审判。

陈先生自称是托洛茨基的追随者，据告知，他曾费心向在此主持首次听证的法官解释他的共产主义类型与目前在苏俄流行的共产主义之间的区别。但这种区别仅是学术性的。在法律眼中，一名共产党员与另一名共产党员同样应受惩罚。无论一个人多么喜欢将共产主义作为一种学说来研究，其针对既定权威和秩序的激进倾向，总会受到一个坦率自称为资本主义社会的谴责。

我无意以任何形式或方式为陈先生辩护。如果警方查获的证据被证实为真实，他将在适当时候因拥护与当前社会秩序相悖的事业而受到相应的判决。

理想主义者

当然，很难将共和国中对民主原则的倡导与对思想和理想的压制调和起来。在公众看来，陈先生似乎是一个有理想并为之献身的人。但任何主张法治的人都不能让情感干扰司法进程。正义可能是也可能不是全世界法学家所追求的理想之近似值，但除非有更好的东西取而代之，否则它必须作为我们日常行为的准则。

正是出于这个原因，公众中公正的部分支持了中国司法机关在诺伦斯案中的行动。出于同样的原因，陈先生的审判将受到密切关注。这既显示不出对他个人的敌意，也不表示无条件同意政府的政策。这仅仅是对现行法律行政管理的认可。

又一暴行

无论陈先生的审判结果如何，讨论未决案件是不允许的。人们不禁想知道，那些曾大声疾呼为诺伦斯夫妇辩护并同样大声谴责现政府的世界知识分子和中国自由派捍卫者们怎么了。

当然，如果说知识界精英支持释放诺伦斯夫妇的国际运动是出于人道主义和人权灵感以外的任何动机，那将是荒谬的。除了他们所代表的事业外，他们对这些“受害者”不可能有任何个人利益。

现在，陈先生发现自己陷入了与诺伦斯夫妇相同的困境，却没有任何人为他发声。如果诺伦斯夫妇值得全世界关注，那么陈先生也应如此，或许对中国人来说更是如此。

作为中国伟大的学者和这个国家曾有过的革命领袖之一，如果有哪位共产党员值得同情，他肯定更值得中国自由派的同情。奇怪的是，唯一表现出兴趣的人是蒋介石将军，他已同意给予这名囚犯兼昔日同志一次良好的听证机会。

我并不是呼吁国家为了陈先生而起而抗议。我没有为诺伦斯夫妇这样呼吁，也不会为他这样做。但我确实要问，为什么那些为了外国共产党员的生命而翻天覆地的人，现在却对这位曾为中国做出良好贡献的中国共产党员表现出如此惊人的冷漠。

陈在受苦

据报道，陈先生患病且衣着不足。当局好心地纠正了这一不足，但人权旗手们并没有抓住这一点，像他们对待所谓诺伦斯夫妇受虐待那样，为他广播令人心碎的悲惨故事来反对政府。

我不知道陈先生是否有孩子，像诺伦斯夫妇那样。如果有，公众并未得知，这可能是由于沉睡的人类自由捍卫者的疏忽。本案的这一人性化层面非常值得调查，我将此建议免费提供给任何相关人士。

两起性质相同的案件中公众反应的差异并非偶然，而是故意的。受害者是外国人，而陈先生不是。中国政府对外国人做什么是一件严重的事情；对中国人的所作所为则无关紧要。这对外国人来说是贬低，但对中国人来说是伤害。如果这种态度出现在普通人身上，还不太严重。但当它出自该国自封的自由思想家之口时，就是我们所有人都该进行一些反思的时候了。

但陈先生的智力状态并不会因他们的行动或不行动而动摇。

（批：oic 8/3）
（批：Apmekin）
（批：D.B.R.）
（批：27/10）

REPORT
Date October 21, 1932.

Subject (in full) Enquiry regarding Chen To Seu and particulars of a
further seizure of communist literature.

Made by D.S.I. Everest. Forwarded by O.Bkn. a.i.

At 10.30 a.m. October 20, during the course of a
visit by the undersigned and Clerk Zung to the residence of
Chen To Seu, No.11 Yung Shing Li, Yochow Road, for the purpose
of making enquiries connected with Chen To Seu's correspondence,
a quantity of communist documents and literature was discovered
in a box in a room adjoining the room in which Chen To Seu
was arrested on October 15.

A list of the documents and literature found is
attached herewith.

The room in which this additional literature was
found is rented by Chen To Seu and, besides being used as a
kitchen, is occupied by an amah in his employ named Shih
Zung Sz (石陈氏). Questioned regarding her employer the
servant stated that the family name of her master is "Li" (李)
and that she understood that he, and her mistress Mrs. Li,
had resided in the rooms for about twelve months, but she
herself had only been in their employ for three months. She
further stated that her mistress was absent when the police
arrested her master on October 15 but that she returned home
the next day and took away a quantity of clothing saying
that she was going to stay for a while with friends in Pootung.

Efforts to ascertain further information regarding
the alias used by Chen To Seu have so far been unsuccessful.
The first tenant of the house, who is responsible for letting
the rooms, left Shanghai for Ningpo in September and is not
expected to return for some weeks, while enquiries among the
neighbours only corroborated the information already obtained
from the servant.

Further enquiries are proceeding.

Officer i/c Special Branch.
D. S. I.
（签名：Everest）

报告
日期：1932年10月21日。

主题（全称） 关于陈独秀的调查及进一步查获共产主义文献的详细情况。

由副督察长 Everest 制作。由代理警官 O.Bkn. 转发。

10月20日上午10时30分，在下级警官和职员 Zung 访问位于约克路永盛里11号的陈独秀住所期间，目的是查询与陈独秀通信有关的事项，在与10月15日逮捕陈独秀的房间相邻的一个房间的箱子里，发现了大量共产主义文件和文献。

所发现的文件和文献清单附后。

发现这些额外文献的房间由陈独秀租用，除用作厨房外，还住着他雇用的一名名叫石陈氏的女佣。当被问及她的雇主时，这名仆人称她主人的姓是“李”，她理解他和女主人李太太在这些房间住了大约十二个月，但她自己只为他们工作了三个月。她还说，10月15日警察逮捕她主人时，女主人不在家，但第二天她回到家，拿走了一批衣物，说要去浦东的朋友家住一段时间。

迄今为止，查明陈独秀所用化名的进一步努力均未成功。负责出租房屋的第一位租户已于9月离开上海前往宁波，预计几周内不会回来，而向邻居进行的查询仅证实了已从仆人那里获得的信息。

进一步调查正在进行中。

特别股主管警官。
副督察长
（签名：Everest）

China Times (Nanking telegram)

THE CASE OF CHEN TOU SEU.

Chen Tou Seu and Pang Zuh Ts arrived at Nanking
by train under armed escort yesterday. They were taken to
the Headquarters of the Central Kuomintang Party where, after
certain arrangements having been made, they were removed to
the Military Court of the Ministry of War for detention.
Over 10 boxes of reactionary literature were sent to the
Central Kuomintang Headquarters for examination, after
which they will be referred to the Military Court to be
dealt with.

Chen Tou Seu and Pang Zuh Ts are at present
in the Detention Room of the Military Court of the Ministry
of War. Chen Tou Seu requested an interview with General
Chiang Kai Shek and Mr. Chen Lih Fu, a member of the Central
Executive Committee of the Kuomintang, to whom he will give
an account of his past activities in the Trotsky party in
China. This request has been accepted by the authorities.
Chen Tou Seu will be brought under escort of the
Military Police on the morning of October 21.

Chen Tou Seu and Pang Zuh Ts arrived at Nanking
under escort on October 20. They will be charged with
acts endangering the Republic of China.

China Times (Soochow telegram)

The action of the Central Kuomintang Head-
quarters in creating a special tribunal to try Chen Tou
Seu being considered a violation of judicial independence,
the Bar Association at Soochow held an urgent meeting on
the afternoon of October 20, at which it was resolved to
despatch the following telegram to the Executive Council
and the Ministry of Judicial Administration at Nanking:-

"Chen Tou Seu should be severely dealt with
for his acts against the Republic of China. However,
newspapers have reported that the Central Kuomintang
Headquarters will create a special tribunal to hear the
case. This association regards such action to be
inexpedient on the ground that such crimes other than
those committed in Bandit Suppression or Martial Law
areas and those committed by militarists are subject
to Special Laws and should be dealt with by the High
Court. For instance, the recent Houlens Case was
tried by the Kiangsu High Court. The Chen Tou Seu
case should be dealt with in a similar manner. The
creation of a special tribunal is liable to cause the
friendly Powers to criticise the Chinese judiciary and
will seriously affect the Government's movement to
abolish extraterritoriality".

《字林西报》（南京电）

陈独秀案。

陈独秀和彭述之昨日在武装护送下乘火车抵达南京。他们被带往国民党中央党部总部，在进行某些安排后，被移送至军政部军事法庭羁押。十箱以上的反动文献已送至国民党中央党部总部审查，随后将移交军事法庭处理。

陈独秀和彭述之目前关押在军政部军事法庭的拘留室。陈独秀请求会见蒋介石将军和国民党中央执行委员陈立夫先生，他将向他们陈述其过去在中国托洛茨基派中的活动情况。当局已接受此请求。陈独秀将于10月21日上午在宪兵护送下被提审。

陈独秀和彭述之于10月20日在护送下抵达南京。他们将被指控犯有危害中华民国罪。

《字林西报》（苏州电）

鉴于国民党中央党部总部设立特别法庭审判陈独秀被视为违反司法独立，苏州律师公会于10月20日下午召开紧急会议，决议向南京行政院和司法行政部发送以下电报：

“陈独秀因危害中华民国之行径应受严惩。然而，据报纸报道，国民党中央党部总部将设立特别法庭审理此案。本会认为此举不妥，理由是除在剿匪或戒严地区所犯罪行及军阀所犯罪行适用特别法并应由高等法院处理外，其他罪行均应由普通法院审理。例如，最近的侯伦案即由江苏高等法院审理。陈独秀案应以类似方式处理。设立特别法庭易招致友好列强对中国司法界的批评，并将严重影响政府废除治外法权的运动。”

page_data.en:
Extract of Daily Intelligence Report dated 18/10/32.

Raids on Communist Bases - result of Court Proceedings

Chen Tou Seu (陳獨秀) and his ten accomplices who were arrested during a series of raids on October 15, 16 and 17 on a charge of propagating communism (Vide I.R. of 17/10/32), appeared in court on October 17, when they were ordered to be handed over to the Chinese Authorities together with the literature seized.
page_data.zh:
1932年10月18日每日情报报告摘录。

突袭共产主义据点 - 法庭诉讼结果

陈独秀及其十名同伙在10月15日、16日和17日的一系列突袭行动中因涉嫌传播共产主义被捕（见1932年10月17日情报报告），于10月17日出庭，当时被命令连同查获的文献一起移交给中国当局。

page_data.en:
Extract from Intelligence Report 18.10.32.
- : -
Case against Chen Tou Jeu et al - one further arrest
As a result of a watch maintained at premises
No. 335 Nyih Kwong Li (業廣里), Tongshan Road, where
two communists were arrested and a large quantity of
literature was seized on October 16, one named Kwoh
Ching Hao (郭銑豪) alias Bang Dau Ts-(彭道之) alias
Borovikoff, native of Hunan was arrested at 3.45 p.m.
October 17 whilst entering the premises. A search of
this individual's place of residence at No. 531 Sieu Tuh
Li (修德里), Burkill Road, made on October 17, resulted
in the finding of a quantity of communist literature.
He will appear before Court on October 18, when
an application for his extradition will be made by the
Chinese Authorities.

由于对唐山路业广里335号 premises 进行了监视，该处于10月16日逮捕了两名共产主义者并查获了大量文献，一名名叫郭铣豪（Kwoh Ching Hao），化名彭道之（Bang Dau Ts-），又名博罗维科夫（Borovikoff）的湖南籍男子，于10月17日下午3点45分进入该处时被捕。10月17日对该人在伯基尔路修德里531号的住所进行的搜查，结果发现了大量共产主义文献。他将于10月18日出庭，届时中国当局将申请引渡他。

For further attention. It will be necessary to :

1. Interview the Legal Department with a view to ascertaining
(a) the character of the evidence which will be required
in order to have the various prisoners handed over to
the Chinese Authorities;
(b) the evidence which will be required, failing the
possibility of having them handed over, to have
them convicted in the Court in the Settlement.

✓ 2. Examine and classify documents and prepare short summary of
contents of documents which constitute important evidence
in the cases against the various accused.

✓ 3. Collect information which will help to prove that various
accused were the real occupiers of the rooms in which they
were arrested and or in which incriminating documents and
literature were found.

4. Collect information on the subject of the weekly or the
monthly expenditure of each of the accused, the source
from which the money was obtained, the banks in which it
was kept or otherwise used by the accused, etc.

5. Ascertain the manner in which the various accused received
mail. Is the accommodation address used by Chen To Seu
known ? Have arrangements been made to seize letters
delivered at his home ? Will the C.P.O. be on the alert
to see if the clearing of any mail box stops as a result of
these arrests ?

6. Keep a dozen specimens of each book, paper or document
which I have marked on the lists of articles found which is
now being copied by S.4. If a dozen is not available keep as
many as can be spared. If only one copy is available please
arrange, if that course is practical, to have it copied or
photographed.

供进一步处理。有必要：

1. 咨询法律部，以查明：
(a) 为将各名囚犯移交给中国当局所需证据的性质；
(b) 若无法移交，为在租界法庭将其定罪所需之证据。

✓ 2. 审查并分类文件，并编制构成针对各被告案件重要证据的文件内容简要摘要。

✓ 3. 收集有助于证明各被告确系其被捕房间和/或发现罪证文件及宣传品房间的 actual 居住者的信息。

4. 收集关于每名被告每周或每月开支、资金来源、存放资金的银行或被被告以其他方式使用的银行等信息。

5. 查明各被告接收邮件的方式。陈独秀（Chen To Seu）使用的通信地址是否已知？是否已安排扣押寄往其家中的信件？中央邮政局（C.P.O.）是否会保持警惕，观察是否有信箱因这些逮捕而停止清理邮件？

6. 保留我在已查获物品清单上标记的每种书籍、报纸或文件的十二份样本，该清单现正由 S.4 抄录。若不足十二份，则保留尽可能多的数量。若仅有一份副本，请在切实可行的情况下安排复制或拍照。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

At 3.45 p.m. 17/10/32 one L'u Ching Hao, age 21, native of Honan was arrested at 335 Myih Kwong Li, Tongehan Road by C.D.C.291 of Wayside Station, who had been posted at that address since the 16/10/32 following a raid carried out by the Special Branch when a quantity of Communistic literature was seized.

The accused was seen by C.D.C.291 to enter the down stairs back room of the above address and finding nobody there he came out and was arrested. The room referred to is the one in which the communistic literature was seized on the 17/10/32. The accused made a statement in which he stated that he arrived at Shanghai from Nanking at 9.00 a.m. 17/10/32.

Subsequent enquiries at 531 Purkill Road proved that the accused has been residing in the room above the kitchen at that address for the past 10 months. He was identified by the main tenant

It was in this room that a quantity of communistic literature was seized by the Special Branch at 2 a.m. on the 17, 10/32. The accused will appear in the S.S.D.Court on the 18/10/32 when the Chinese Authorities will made application for him to be handed over.

调查记录。

1932年10月17日下午3时45分，一名名叫陆清浩（L'u Ching Hao，音译）、21岁、河南籍的男子，在通汗路（Tongehan Road，音译）倪广里335号被路边巡捕房的 C.D.C.291 号警员逮捕。该警员自1932年10月16日起便在该地址蹲守，此前特别处进行了一次突袭行动，缴获了大量共产主义宣传品。

C.D.C.291 号警员目睹被告进入上述地址的后楼下房间，发现屋内无人后，被告走出房间并被逮捕。所述房间即为1932年10月17日缴获共产主义宣传品的房间。被告作出一份陈述，称其于1932年10月17日上午9时从南京抵达上海。

随后在伯基尔路（Burkill Road）531号的查询证实，被告在过去10个月内一直居住在该地址厨房楼上的房间内。主要租户对其进行了指认

特别处于1932年10月17日凌晨2时在该房间缴获了大量共产主义宣传品。被告将于1932年10月18日出庭受审，届时中国当局将申请将其移交。

（批注：1. P. 1932年10月18日 JR）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Kuo Ching-hao (郭鏡豪) alias Pang Tao-ts
(彭道之)
native of Hunan taken by me D.I. Ross
at S.2., S.B. on the Oct. 17, 1932 and interpreted by D.I.Sih Tse-liang

My name is Kuo Ching-hao (郭鏡豪) alias Pang Tao-ts 彭道之, native of Lo Ho Tsung
(羅河村) Village, Chao Yang (朝陽) Hsien, Hunan, age 21,
married. After studying in a private school at my native place
for four years I entered a primary school in the same village.
I completed my studies there three years later and became a
teacher in the same school for one year. In January, 16th
year (1927) I enrolled in the Yoeh-Yung (岳雲) Middle School,
Changsha, Hunan. Two years later I proceeded to Shanghai and
studied as a boarding student in the Labour University, Kiangwan.
In August, 1931 I joined the Arts Course in the Chinan
University, Chenju as the Labour University had been closed
down by order of the National Government. I remained in
Chinan University till January, 1932 when the school suspended
studies owing to the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Chapei. I
was then introduced by a schoolmate named Liu Peng-tseng
(劉奉正) to his friend named Chen Dah-ko (陳大可) who was
a teacher in the Kiang-Che (江浙) Primary School, 39 Yung
Chong Li (榮昌里), East Yuhang Road where he stayed. I stayed
with Chen for about two months and then left Shanghai by the
s.s. "Ningshao" for Hankow and returned native place by train.
In July 1932 I left my home and stayed with a countryman named
Er Yang-hwa (歐陽華) in Changsha who is a paint dealer. Two
months later, on or about September 28 I left alone Changsha
by train and came to Hankow where I boarded the s.s. "Anking"
and came to Nanking. I completed my journey to Shanghai by
train arriving here at 9 a.m. to-day, October 17. At the
Shanghai North I was met by Liu Peng-tseng (劉奉正) (who

警方调查报告。

以下为郭镜豪（Kuo Ching-hao），别名彭道之（Pang Tao-ts），湖南籍人士的供词，由我（督察 Ross）于1932年10月17日在特别处 S.2 室录取，并由督察施子良（Sih Tse-liang）翻译。

我叫郭镜豪，别名彭道之，籍贯湖南朝阳县罗河村，21岁，已婚。在家乡私塾读书四年后，我进入同村的一所小学。三年后完成学业，并在该校任教一年。民国十六年（1927年）一月，我考入湖南长沙岳云中学。两年后前往上海，在江湾劳动大学作为寄宿生就读。1931年8月，由于国民政府下令关闭劳动大学，我转入真如暨南大学文科课程学习。我在暨南大学一直待到1932年1月，当时因闸北中日战事学校停课。随后，经一位名叫刘奉正的同学介绍，我认识了他的朋友陈大可，陈是位于余杭东路荣昌里39号的江浙小学的教员，我便住在他那里。我与陈同住了约两个月，随后乘“宁绍”轮离开上海前往汉口，并乘火车返回家乡。1932年7月，我离开家，在长沙与一位名叫欧阳华的同乡同住，他是油漆商。两个月后，即9月28日左右，我独自乘火车离开长沙前往汉口，在那里登上“安庆”轮来到南京。我乘火车完成至上海的旅程，于今天，10月17日上午9时抵达此处。在上海北站，我见到了刘奉正（他

Raids on Communist Bases - 11 arrests

A series of raids on important communist bases in the Settlement and French Concession were made by the Special Branch of the Municipal Police on October 15, 16 and 17, 1932, resulting in the arrest of Chen Tou-seu (陈独秀), one of the founders of the Chinese Communist Party and leader of the Leftist Opposition Clique and ten other important members of the Chinese Communist Party, and the seizure of large quantities of important documents and communist literature in the Chinese, Japanese and Russian languages.

In addition to the Stalin Clique, the Leftist Opposition Clique or the Trotsky Clique played an important part in communist activities among the labouring and poor masses in Shanghai and other parts of the country and as a result of the raids on the bases of this Clique, which was made possible by the expeditious manner in which they were conducted, communist activities in Shanghai will be considerably weakened and the Trotsky Clique having lost its leaders will undoubtedly remain inactive for some time. The particulars of the raids are given hereunder:

1. No.210 Tsung Yang Li (□□□), East Yuhang Road
Acting on the authority of a warrant issued at the request of the Public Safety Bureau, the Municipal Police at 2.30 p.m. October 15 raided the Headquarters of the Leftist Opposition Clique of the Chinese Communist Party at No.210 Tsung Yang Li, East Yuhang Road, where five members of the Standing Committee were holding an important meeting in an upstairs room. These five communists were taken into custody and large quantity of communist documents and propaganda matter seized. The names of the arrested persons are as follows :-
Zia Siou-san (谢少珊), aged 23, native of Canton.
Wang Tsau-jung (王兆群), aged 27 native of Anhwei.
Poh Yih-van (濮一凡), aged 28, native of Anhwei.
Tsang Tscu-nyoeh (张次山), native of Anhwei.
Bang Zuh-ts (彭述之), native of Anhwei.
As a result of information obtained during the course of this raid, the undermentioned addresses were visited with the following results :-
2. No.11 Yung Shing Li (永兴里), Yochow Road
Chen Tou-seu (陈独秀), a noted communist leader, was arrested at this address and a search of his room resulted in the seizure of a large quantity of communist documents and other Red literature. He was found to be indisposed and, after his arrest, he was immediately sent to the Police Hospital where he was found to be suffering from enteritis.
3) No.322 Kan Foh Li, Route des Soeurs, French Concession
This address was raided at 9 p.m. October 15. A large quantity of communist literature was seized and one Wong Siao-tsurig (王晓光) arrested.
4) No.1044 Sz Wen Li (斯文里), Tatung Road
A raid carried out at 12.50 a.m. October 16 on this address unearthed a large quantity of literature and caused the arrest of one Jiang Yeu-kong (江有公).
5) No.355 Nyih Kwo Li (二国里), Tongshan Road
This place was raided at 7.30 p.m. October 16 and a large quantity of communist literature together with two myriograph duplicators were seized. Two self-confessed communists named Woc Ah-fong (何阿芳) alias Woo Ts-sung (伍子松) and Wong Ts-bing (王丙) alias Tsung Mang (宗孟) found in the room were arrested. This address was used as the publication office of the Leftist Opposition Clique.
6) House No.22, Passage 456, Rue Prelupt, French Concession
At 12 midnight October 16/17, a visit to this place in company with the French Police revealed a large quantity of communist literature and one Wong Chien-dong (王鉴东) alias Wong Liang-tong (王良栋) found on the premises was arrested.
7) 531 Kirkhill Road
A raid was made at this address at 2 a.m. October 17 and a quantity of literature seized. The occupant of the room was absent at the time of the raid.
The eleven accused will appear before Court on October 17 when an application for their extradition to the Chinese authorities will be made.

突袭共产党据点——逮捕11人

1932年10月15日、16日和17日，工部局警务处政治部对租界及法租界内的重要共产党据点实施了一系列突袭行动，结果逮捕了中国共产党创始人之一、左派反对派领袖陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu）及其他十名中国共产党重要成员，并缴获了大量中文、日文和俄文的重要文件及共产主义文献。

除了斯大林派系外，左派反对派或称托洛茨基派在上海及全国其他地区的劳工和贫苦民众的共产主义活动中发挥了重要作用。由于对该派系据点的突袭行动迅速高效，上海的共产主义活动将大大削弱，而托洛茨基派因失去领导人，无疑将在一段时间内处于停滞状态。突袭详情如下：

1. 东余杭路宗杨里（Tsung Yang Li，□□□）210号
根据公共安全局的要求签发的搜查令授权，工部局警务处于10月15日下午2时30分突袭了位于东余杭路宗杨里210号的中国共产党左派反对派总部，当时五名常务委员正在楼上房间举行重要会议。这五名共产党员被拘留，并缴获了大量共产主义文件和宣传材料。被捕人员姓名如下：
谢少珊（Zia Siou-san），23岁，广东籍。
王兆群（Wang Tsau-jung），27岁，安徽籍。
濮一凡（Poh Yih-van），28岁，安徽籍。
张次山（Tsang Tscu-nyoeh），安徽籍。
彭述之（Bang Zuh-ts），安徽籍。
根据此次突袭过程中获得的情报，警方走访了以下地址，结果如下：
2. 耀州路永兴里（Yung Shing Li）11号
著名共产党领袖陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu）在此地址被捕，对其房间的搜查导致缴获大量共产主义文件和其他红色文献。发现其身体不适，被捕后立即送往警务处医院，确诊患有肠炎。
3) 法租界修女路（Route des Soeurs）甘福里（Kan Foh Li）322号
该地址于10月15日晚9时被突袭。缴获大量共产主义文献，并逮捕王晓光（Wong Siao-tsurig）一人。
4) 大通路斯文里（Sz Wen Li）1044号
10月16日凌晨12时50分对该地址进行突袭，查获大量文献，并逮捕江有公（Jiang Yeu-kong）一人。
5) 唐山路二国里（Nyih Kwo Li）355号
该处于10月16日晚7时30分被突袭，缴获大量共产主义文献及两台油印机。在房间内发现的两名自认是共产党员的人，即何阿芳（Woc Ah-fong），化名伍子松（Woo Ts-sung），以及王丙（Wong Ts-bing），化名宗孟（Tsung Mang），均被逮捕。该地址被用作左派反对派的出版办公室。
6) 法租界普鲁帕特路（Rue Prelupt）456弄22号
10月16/17日午夜12时，与法国警察一同前往该处，发现大量共产主义文献，并在现场逮捕王鉴东（Wong Chien-dong），化名王良栋（Wong Liang-tong）一人。
7) 柯克希尔路（Kirkhill Road）531号
10月17日凌晨2时对该地址进行突袭，缴获部分文献。突袭时房间 occupant（居住者）不在场。
十一名被告将于10月17日出庭，届时将申请将其引渡给中国当局。

At 12 M.N. October 16/17 another raid was executed
with the assistance of the French Police on house No.22,
Passage 456, Rue Frelupt, which resulted in the arrest of one
Wong Chien Dong (于鑑堂) alias Wong Liang Tong (王良栋) and the
seizure of a quantity of communist literature including seven
sheets of carbon paper containing an article entitled "An open
letter to the whole body of Comrades in Shanghai."
At 2 a.m. October 17 a search of the room above the
kitchen at No.531 Sieu Tuh Lee (修德里), Burkhill Road, produced
a quantity of communist literature. The tenant was absent
at the time of the raid and according to a note which was
found pinned on the door there is little likelihood of his
returning to this address. The note contains a message from
one Kwoh Jing Hao (郭競豪) addressed to Bai Wan (培文)
warning him not to visit Sz Vai's (世凡) place owing to
certain happenings and advising him to go and stay with some
friend at once.
Appended herewith are copies of lists of the various
documents etc. seized at the abovementioned places together
with copies of statements made by the eleven accused. These
individuals will be brought before court on October 17, when

The first named Zai Siau-san admitted after
arrest that the five men constituted the standing
committee of the Chinese Communist Party,
Leftist Opposition Clique and met at that address
about once a week to discuss the problems and
policies of the party. He also admitted that
he was the tenant of room in which the
seizure was made and that he was temporarily
acting for one Chen Tou-seu (陈独秀), who he
claimed was sick, but who in ordinary circumstances
was the leader of the Trotsky or Leftist Opposition
Clique in China. The five persons in custody
together with the seized literature were removed
to Kashing Road Station and later to Police
Headquarters where they were interrogated. As
the result of this interrogation it was learned
that an important member of the party was
residing at No.11 Yung Shing Li, off Yochow Road.
This address was raided at 6.45 p.m. on October
15, with the further assistance of detectives
from Wayside Station. In an upstairs front
room, one male Chinese, the 6th accused Chen Tou-
seu (陈独秀), was arrested and a large quantity
of communist literature and documents seized from
drawers and boxes in various parts of the room
(translations attached).

第一名被告谢少珊（Zai Siau-san）被捕后承认，这五个人构成了中国共产党左翼反对派的常务委员会，并大约每周在该地址聚会一次，讨论党的问题和政策。他还承认他是进行搜查的房间的租户，并且他暂时代理陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu），他声称陈生病了，但在通常情况下，陈是中国托洛茨基派或左翼反对派的领袖。五名在押人员连同缴获的文献被带往嘉善路分局，随后带往警察总局接受审讯。审讯结果显示，一名重要的党员居住在姚州路（Yochow Road）旁的永興里11号。10月15日下午6:45，在路边分局侦探的进一步协助下，对该地址进行了突袭。在楼上的一间前房里，逮捕了一名中国男子，即第六名被告陈独秀（Chen Tou-seu），并从房间各处的抽屉和箱子中缴获了大量共产主义文献和文件（附有译文）。

1932年10月16日凌晨12:50，在大通路旁的斯文里（Sz Vung Li）1044号，逮捕了第八名被告梁有光（Liang Yeu-kwang），并从房间的书桌和箱子中缴获了一批共产主义文献。由于时间较晚，在进入房屋时发出了一些噪音，当强行打开上述被捕者所占房间的门时，他和另一名中国男子从窗户跳入下面的弄堂逃跑。签署人跳下追赶这些人并成功实施了逮捕，从而阻止了梁有光的逃脱。随即对邻近地区进行了搜查以寻找第二名男子，但无果。梁有光被问及同伴的身份，但拒绝提供任何信息。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Zia Tuh Pang (Zia Siao San)
native of Kwangtung taken by me D.S.I. Golder
at Police Hdqrs. on the 16-10-32 and interpreted by Clerk Liao Tsong Chien.

My name is Zia Tuh Pang (謝篤生) alias Zia
Siao San (謝小珊). I was born in the city of Canton
in 1911, thus being 21 years of age. Until I was
five years of age I lived with my father, who was
an engineer in a silk weaving factory in Canton.
Entering the Yi Ling Miao Primary School (藝林廟)
at 5 years of age I remained there until I had attain-
ed my ninth year, my father then transferred me
to the 1st Primary School established by the Canton
Municipality. After 3 years of study I was sent to
the 1st Middle School founded by the Kwangtung
Province at Canton. Three years later I graduated
from the Junior Department and was at that time a
member of the Kuomintang Party. (that is in 1925)
Shortly before the rupture between the Kuomintang and
the Communist Party I joined the Communist Youth.
Group, and under the aegis of this organization was
sent to study in the Eastern University in Moscow.
Normally students under the age of 20 are not admitted
to the Eastern University, but I had been singled out
by the Communist Youth Group who altered my age.
During my stay in Moscow I studied Russian, History,
Philosophy, and Economics, the last subject being
given first place in importance. On leaving Canton
the party of which I was a member consisted of 6
students, but on arrival at Shanghai the group were
augmented by some 50 others all of whom were bound

以下是我，副督察长戈尔登（D.S.I. Golder），于1932年10月16日在警察总局对广东籍人士谢笃生（Zia Tuh Pang，又名谢小珊 Zia Siao San）进行的讯问笔录，由职员廖宗建（Liao Tsong Chien）翻译。

我叫谢笃生（Zia Tuh Pang），又名谢小珊（Zia Siao San）。我于1911年出生在广州城，现年21岁。直到五岁为止，我与父亲同住，父亲是广州一家丝织厂的工程师。五岁时我进入艺林庙（Yi Ling Miao）小学，在那里一直读到九岁，随后父亲将我转学到广州市立第一小学。经过三年的学习，我被送入广东省立广州第一中学。三年后我从初中部毕业，当时我是国民党党员。（那是1925年）在国共破裂前不久，我加入了共产主义青年团，并在该组织的资助下被派往莫斯科东方大学学习。通常东方大学不招收20岁以下的学生，但我被共产主义青年团特别选中，他们修改了我的年龄。在莫斯科期间，我学习了俄语、历史、哲学和经济学，其中经济学被列为最重要的科目。离开广州时，我所在的团体由6名学生组成，但在抵达上海时，该团体增加了约50人，所有人都前往

For the same destination. Many of them were actually
members of the Kuomintang Party and entered the Sun
Yat sen University in Moscow on their arrival.
During the latter part of 1929 I met and married
Tsung Zau Lan ( 曾左蘭 ), a native of Hupeh who
was a student in the Sun Yat-sen University, but
who since returning to China has renounced her
connection with politics entirely. After 18 months
study at the Eastern University I was transferred to
the Sun Yat Sen foundation to act as interpreter
for the classes of Chinese then going through in the
University. Soon after my transfer the Eastern
University was closed owing to the students evincing
opposition to the "Miff" or "Far Eastern Affairs Section".
80% of the students returned to China but the remainder
embraced the Soviet teachings and went over to the
Sun Yat Sen University. During the end of 1929
the Communist Party proper became formed into two
cliques, the Trotsky and Aladin factions. As a result
of taking sides 20 students including myself were dis-
missed from study and returned to China. I had leaned
towards the teachings of Trotsky as had the remainder
of those returning home. It must be explained that the
most powerful of the heads of the Soviet at that time
was Stalin who would not allow the formations of
of internal factions.

1929年下半年，我结识并娶了曾左蘭（Tsung Zau Lan），她是湖北人，曾是孙逸仙大学的学生，但自回到中国后已完全断绝与政治的联系。在东方大学学习18个月后，我被调至孙逸仙基金会，担任当时在大学上课的中国学生的翻译员。在我调职后不久，由于学生表现出反对“米夫”（Miff）或“远东事务处”，东方大学被关闭。80%的学生返回中国，但其余的人接受了苏维埃学说，转入了孙逸仙大学。1929年底，正式的共产党分裂成两个派系，即托洛茨基派和阿拉丁派（Aladin factions，原文如此，可能指布哈林或其他派系音译）。由于站队问题，包括我在内的20名学生被开除学籍并返回中国。我和其他回国者一样，倾向于托洛茨基的学说。必须说明的是，当时苏联最有权势的领导人是斯大林，他不允许内部派系的形成。

Upon arriving at Vladivostok, I took steamer to
Shanghai, arriving here in early part of 1930, when I
took up my residence with one Woo Hyi-yieh (吴季严),
a follower of Trotsky who was living at 1575 Faung
Yuen Li, Tongshan Road. Woo employed me to translate
"A History of the German Federation" from Russian to
Chinese. For this work I was paid $30 to $40 per
month. The draft of the book was later handed to
the Zung Chow Kuo Kwang Book Store, Honan Road, for
publication, but so far has not been put into print.
After residing with Woo for about 1 year, I went into
a room of my own at No.61 Jin Sing Li, Ward Road. At
this time I had already come into contact with Chen
Teu-sou who at a meeting held at No.160 Tshung Yang
Li, East Yuhang Road, which was attended by Lou Han (罗汉),
Bang Zuh-ts (彭述之). Woo Kyi-yieh (吴季严) gave me
permission to take up my residence at 160 Tshung Yang
Li, East Yuhang Road and noted that I should be paid
sufficient to maintain myself. When I had been living
at 160 Tshung Yang Li for a period of three months, the
Sino-Japanese hostilities broke out so that I moved to
No.20 Chi Yuan Terrace (纪园), Connaught Road.
One month after the district became safe I took up
quarters at No.210 Tshung Yang Li, East Yuhang Road,
which address was used as a meeting place. Until
about one month ago when Chen Teu Sou fell ill he

When 10 years of age I entered a private school in Tsongchow where
I studied for 3 years after which I entered the Second Middle
School in the same city. I left the school when I was 16 years
of age and I was living with my uncle who has a farm near the
Tsongchow Hsien until about October 12, 1932 when I left for
Shanghai. The reason of my leaving my native place was because
I was illtreated by my uncle named Wong Tuh Shien (王德宣) who
is senior member of my family. I had $29 in my possession when
I left Tsongchow and I spent $28 on my way to Shanghai. I
arrived here about 6 p.m. October 14, 1932 and spent the whole
night walking on streets as I had no money and no friends and
relatives in Shanghai. At about 12 noon October 15 I met a
fellow country man of mine named Lieu King Piao (刘金彪) whom I
knew when I was a boy. I asked Lieu to help me to find an
employment. He promised to do so and took me to a house (No.210
(Tsung Yang Li, East Yuhang Road)(I do not know the name of the
street) arriving there at about 1 p.m. Upon entering the house
we went into an upst-irs room where we found two persons named
Zia and Wong, to whom I was introduced by Lieu. Lieu then left
telling me to wait until he returns. A few minutes after his
departure another two men, whose names names I do not known,
entered the room. They all smoked cigarettes and asked me
questions as to who I was and why I had come to Shanghai. At
about 2.30 p.m. the police arrived and all of us were under

My name is Tsang Tseu Nyoeh ( 張次南 ), age 34, M/teacher,
native of Anhwei. Up to the age of 11 years I studied
Chinese at my native place, Hweichow ( 徽州 ) Anhwei Province.
I then entered the Tsung Tseong ( 正中 ) Primary School
in the same town. After two years at this school I left
Hweichow with my mother and joined the Li Ngoh ( 旅鄂 ) Middle
School in Woochang. I remained in this school for 18
months and then, because of my father's death, I left and
travelled to Changsha, entering the Min Tuh ( 明德 ) Middle
School, where I studied for another two years. At the
end of the period I went to Peiping with my uncle and secured
employment as a tutor to Li Ts Fang ( 李子 ), Ts Kai Kuo
Terrace (number forgotten). After 3 years at this
employ I went to Mukden. There I stayed three months.
Unable to find a position I returned to Peiping and studied
at the University there for about two years. After this
I was a teacher in the Kung Teh ( 孔德 ) Primary School
for two or three years. I then went to Wuhan in Hupeh
in search of employment. After 6 months in Wuhan, during
which period I was unemployed, I came to Shanghai. This
was about 8 years ago. I put up at 13 Tsung Shing Li ( 正興里 )
Chapei and remained at this address for three or four months,
When I went back to Peiping. After a few months in Peiping
I went to Tientsin as a teacher in Tientsin Middle School.
I was at this post for 6 months and then returned to Peiping
once more. For two and half years I worked as a teacher
in the Shee San ( 西山 ) Middle School, Peiping. When

My name is Pu Ih Van, aged 28, male, native of Anhwe.
I reside at No.3 2 Kau Fon Li (两福里), Route des Soeurs. I
am a graduate of the Arts Department of the University of Waseda
in Tokyo where I had studied for four years. I came to Shanghai
in 1930. I translated Japanese novels and contributed to the
Cheng Chow Kwoh Kwong Zeu (神州国光社) Book Store on Honan Road.
Li Z San (李次山), a lawyer residing at No.7 Datung Road,
introduced me to Li Kwo Zeh (李国杰), President of the China
Merchants Steamship Co. for employment. I was engaged by the
Company in June, 1932 as a member of the editorial staff of the
"China Merchants Monthly Review," with a salary of $170 per
mensem. As I had received instructions from the president to
employ a proof-reader for the Review, I went to No.210 Tsung Yang
Li, East Yuhang Road, to inform Tsang Chun Wei (曾昭偉) aged 20,
of the vacancy because I was asked to get a job for him by one of
my friends named Soo Cho Ching (苏少卿), who left for Yunnan
10 days ago. Tsang was not in the premises and his brother-in-
law named Shia (谢 ) told me to wait as he would come soon.
There were five persons including Shia and myself and he told me
to make myself at home as they were simply talking about a matter
concerning a primary school. After a while a party of police
arrived and arrested me together with others. I visited the
premises for the first time and I have no knowledge of all the
persons arrested. This is my true statement.

Signed: Pol Yik Van.

我叫 Pu Ih Van，28岁，男，籍贯安徽。我居住在姐妹路 (Route des Soeurs) 两福里 ( Kau Fon Li ) 3号。我是东京早稻田大学文学部的毕业生，曾在那里学习了四年。我于1930年来到上海。我翻译日本小说，并向河南路的神州国光社 ( Cheng Chow Kwoh Kwong Zeu ) 书店投稿。居住在大通路7号的律师 Li Z San (李次山) 将我介绍给招商局总裁 Li Kwo Zeh (李国杰) 以求职。1932年6月，我被该公司聘用为《招商月刊》编辑人员，月薪170元。由于接到总裁指示要为该月刊聘请一名校对员，我便前往东余杭路春陽里210号，将这一空缺告知20岁的 Tsang Chun Wei (曾昭偉)，因为我的朋友 Soo Cho Ching (苏少卿) 让我帮他找份工作，而该朋友已于10天前前往云南。Tsang 不在寓所内，他的姐夫姓 Shia (谢 ) 的人让我稍等，说他很快就会回来。包括 Shia 和我在内共有五人，他让我不要拘束，因为他们只是在谈论一所小学的相关事宜。过了一会儿，一队警察到达，将我和其他人一起逮捕。我是第一次访问该寓所，对所有被捕人员均不认识。这是我的真实供词。

The following is the statement of Wang Shao-jung (王兆祥)
native of Nansuchow, Anhwei taken by me D.P.S. Pitts
at Sp. Branch on the 16/10/32 and interpreted by Clerk Kao Yen-keng

My name is Wang Shao-chun (王兆祥), native of Nansuchow,
Anhwei, age 27 and single. I am a teacher by profession
and am at present unemployed. I understand English
a little. When I was 11, I entered the First
Primary School at my native place. I stayed there
for three years. When I was 14, I entered the Fourth
Agricultural School in my native place. I graduated
from this school when I was 18 and then continued my
studies in agriculture at the South Eastern University
at Nanking, where I remained for one year. After
leaving the South Eastern University, I made my way to
Peking where I intended to seek employment as an
agricultural instructor. In this quest, however, I
was unsuccessful, and after remaining in Peking for one
year where my friend Lieu Kwang-yu (刘光宇), a teacher
in the Middle School Department of the Peiping Agricultural
University, supported me, I returned to my native place.
I remained here until I was 25, being unemployed and being
supported by my parents. During this period, I spent
most of my time in self education.
In January 1931, through the recommendation of
Tsai Chong-ying, Athletic director in the Woochang
University, Woochang, I was enabled to secure a position
as a school teacher in the Lieu Ngoeh (旅鄂) Middle School
at Woochang. I remained in this capacity until the
summer vacation of 1932, during which period my monthly
salary was $80.00.

我叫 Wang Shao-chun (王兆祥)，籍贯安徽南宿州，27岁，未婚。我的职业是教师，目前失业。我懂一点英语。11岁时，我进入老家第一小学。在那里呆了三年。14岁时，我进入老家第四农业学校。18岁时从该校毕业，随后在南京东南大学继续攻读农业，在那里呆了一年。离开东南大学后，我前往北京，打算谋求农业讲师的职位。然而，此次求职未果，在北京停留一年后，在我的朋友、北平农业大学中学部教师 Lieu Kwang-yu (刘光宇) 的资助下，我返回老家。我在这里一直待到25岁，期间失业，由父母供养。在此期间，我大部分时间用于自学。
1931年1月，通过武昌武汉大学体育主任 Tsai Chong-ying 的推荐，我得以在武昌 Li Ngoeh (旅鄂 ) 中学获得教师职位。我一直担任此职直到1932年暑假，在此期间我的月薪为80.00元。

                brother
my younger/Wong Shao-loong.    After our meeting, a

In order to request him to recommend me a job.    He

My true name is Chen To Seu (陈独秀). I was born in the year 1879 in the city of Anking, Anwhei Province. My father died when I was age one. I was educated by private tutor at my native place until I was twenty years of age when my mother sent me to Japan so that I could learn the Japanese language in order that I could enter the Nippon University at Tokyo. I studied Japanese for two or three years and then entered the Nippon University. There I studied law, political science and economics. I can read, write and speak Japanese and read and speak a little English. I returned to China about 1910 and resided in Shanghai. I supported myself by teaching in various schools in Shanghai and Hangchow and also by writing educational books. In the year 1912 by reason of the opposition to the Nationalist Party by Yuan Shi Kai I returned to Japan and resumed my studies at the Nippon University, Tokyo. I returned to Shanghai in 1915 and became the editor of a monthly publication entitled "The New Youth" (新青年). The paper opposed militarism, confucianism and all religions and was published by the Jung Yih (群益) Bookstore, Honan Road. In 1916 I was appointed Dean of the Literary College of the Peking University by Dr. Tsai Yu Bai (蔡元培). I remained in Peking until 1920 when I left owing to my opposition to the then Premier of China, Tuan Chi Jui (段祺瑞). I returned to Shanghai and studied socialism and resumed the publication of the "New Youth" (群益) which had been discontinued by the Jung Yih Bookstore. I had an office in Rue de Consulat and lived with my wife and two sons at No. 2 Yu Yang Li (渔阳里), Route Vallon. In October

我的真名是 Chen To Seu (陈独秀)。我于1879年出生在安徽省安庆市。我一岁时父亲去世。我在老家由私塾老师教育，直到二十岁，母亲送我去日本，以便我能学习日语，从而进入东京的日本大学 ( Nippon University )。我学习了两年或三年日语，然后进入日本大学。在那里我学习法律、政治学和经济学。我能读、写、说日语，并能读和说一点英语。我大约在1910年回到中国，居住在上海。我靠在上海和杭州的各种学校教书以及编写教育书籍来维持生计。1912年，由于袁世凯反对国民党，我返回日本，在东京日本大学恢复学业。1915年我回到上海，成为名为《新青年》 ( The New Youth ) 的月刊编辑。该刊物反对军国主义、儒家思想和所有宗教，由河南路的群益书社 ( Jung Yih ) 出版。1916年，我被蔡元培博士 ( Dr. Tsai Yu Bai ) 任命为北京大学文学院院长。我一直留在北京直到1920年，因反对当时的中国总理段祺瑞 ( Tuan Chi Jui ) 而离开。我回到上海，研究社会主义，并恢复了此前由群益书社停刊的《新青年》 ( New Youth ) 的出版。我在领事馆路 ( Rue de Consulat ) 设有一间办公室，并与妻子及两个儿子住在万隆路 ( Route Vallon ) 渔阳里 ( Yu Yang Li ) 2号。十月

1921 I was arrested by the French Police and charged with publishing inflammatory literature. I was fined $100.00 and the office at Rue de Consulat was sealed. A little time later I was appointed Commissioner of Education at Canton. I remained in Canton about nine months. Whilst I was there I joined the Chinese Communist Party but because of my poor health I returned to Shanghai in August 1922. During the same month I was again arrested by the French Police on a similar charge to the previous one and fined a sum of money. It was about this time that I was elected Chief Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and in this capacity I directed the activities of the whole of the Chinese Communist Party under direct instructions from Moscow until 1927. From 1922 until 1927 with the exception of trips to Canton, Hankow and Peking I resided in Shanghai. I changed my address fairly often but most of the time I resided in Chapei. About April 1927 I was dismissed from the post of Chief Secretary of the C.C.P. because of Chiang Kai-shek's anti-communist tendencies for which I was held responsible. A few months afterwards I received orders to proceed to Moscow and because I refused to obey this order I was expelled from the Party altogether. During the time I was Chief Secretary of the C.C.P. I assisted in the organization of the labourers and peasants unions throughout the country, the reorganization of the Kuomintang and the Southern Army and finally in the Northern Expedition of 1926/7. I was in Hankow with Borodin and Li Lih San in 1927.

1921 年，我被法国巡捕逮捕，被控出版煽动性刊物。我被罚款 100.00 元，且位于领事馆路（Rue de Consulat）的办事处被封存。不久后，我被任命为广州教育委员。我在广州停留了约九个月。在此期间，我加入了中国共产党，但因健康状况不佳，我于 1922 年 8 月返回上海。同月，我再次因与上次类似的指控被法国巡捕逮捕，并被处以一笔罚款。大约就在此时，我当选为中国共产党总书记，并在此职位上，根据莫斯科的直接指示，指导整个中国共产党的活动，直至 1927 年。从 1922 年至 1927 年，除了前往广州、汉口和北京的行程外，我均居住在上海。我的住址变更相当频繁，但大部分时间我居住在闸北。1927 年 4 月左右，因蒋介石的反共倾向，而我被认为对此负有责任，故被免去中国共产党总书记职务。几个月后，我接到前往莫斯科的命令，因我拒绝服从该命令，我被彻底开除出党。在我担任中国共产党总书记期间，我协助组织了全国的劳工和农民协会，改组了国民党及南方军队，并最终参与了 1926/7 年的北伐。1927 年，我与鲍罗廷（Borodin）和李立三（Li Lih San）同在汉口。

My name is Wong Ts Ping (王之平) alias Tsung
Mang, 28 years of age, native of Wenchow, Chekiang
Province, married. My home address is Mo Aung Zung Ka
(杜公館桥), Wenchow.

At 6 years of age I entered the Chih Z (志士)
Primary School at the above village. After 3 years
at this school I left and went to Yoong Kya Higher
Primary School, where I remained for four years.
I then studied for 3 years at the 10th Middle
School, founded by Chekiang Province. After 2 or 3
years of unemployment I got a job as clerk at Tsierju
Yamen in the same province. As this place was infested
with bandits I left after one month and returned home.
After a few months unemployed at home I went to Canton,
where I made an unsuccessful application for a cadetship
at the Whampoa Military Academy. However, I obtained
a position as clerk at this Academy, which I held for
6 months. I then left and became engaged as clerk
at the Canton Federation of Labour Unions. As the pay
was very little I resigned after one month. Altogether
I was in Canton for about 3 years.

In April 1927 I left Canton and came to Shanghai
with a recommendation from my friend Sung Ting Yu (秦丁郁)
living in Yung Ming Road ( ), Canton for employ-
ment with Sung Yung Tong ( ) Printing Shop, Klangwan
Road, Chapei. I was employed at this place for 10 months
as a proof reader. While employed there I became acquainted

with Au Kyi (袁千), a sub-manager of the Printing

instance I agreed to join the Communist Party. In
October 1927 I was sent to Moscow, via Vladivostock,
on a Russian steamer by Au Kyi. On the ship Uo Sz
Li (胡士廉), a native of Hunan, took charge of me
and a party of about twenty other Chinese, bound for
the same destination. After a voyage lasting twenty
days we all arrived at Moscow and immediately entered
the Sun Yat Sen University. After studying there for
10 months I fell sick and was sent back to Shanghai
together with six other Chinese students, two of whom
were females. Lieu Kyung Sung (劉景宋) who was of the
Party, is at present a committee member of the Stalin
Clique of the Chinese Communist Party.

It was in January 1929 that I returned to
Shanghai. Shortly after my return I met Oo Ching Woong
(胡慶忠), committee member of the Stalin Clique. He
intended employing me, but changed his mind later,
saying that I had been in communication with the
Leftist Opposition Clique. As a matter of fact, I
had only become acquainted with some of the Clique.
Because of this allegation I was expelled from the Stalin

The following is the statement of Woo Ah Yong (何阿芳)
native of Chekiang taken by me D.P.S. Jones
at Headquarters on the 17/10/'32 and interpreted by Clerk Chen Hung.

My name is Woo Ah Fong alias Woo Fong alias Woo
Ts King(何阿芳又名何芳又名何子錦), age 26, native of
Chekiang, married. My nativeplace is Mienchmen village
(岩川村), Zae An Hsien(瑞安縣) near Wenchow. Up to
the a ge of 14 years I studied Chinese under a village tutor.
I then went to a normal school in Wenchow, where I was a
student for 4½ years. After leaving school I taught for
one year at a Primary School in my native village. I
had a friend named King Zah Sung(金先生 ) in Shanghai who
invited me to join him. So I left for Shanghai in June,
1926. King was employed as secretary at the District
Headquarters of the Kuomintang in Shanghai. I assisted
King at his home in Chapei, printing Kuomintang documents and
letters. In February, 1927, I met King Mo Han(金華韓)
student of the Shanghai University, Chapei. This man
belonged to the Communication Bureau of the Communist Party.
Shortly after making his acquaintance I joined the party and
was employed as messenger by the Communication Bureau at a
salary of $25 per month. I was still working for King
Zah Sung and living with him in Chapei. In September,
1927, the Communist Party sent me to the Eastern University
in Moscow. I studied there for 1 year and was then
transferred to the Sun Yat Sen University in the same city,
where I remained for two years studying communist matters.
For 6 months after leaving the University I worked as a
brasssmith in a Red Politarian Factory in Moscow. At
the end of this period I was obliged to leave the country

以下为浙江籍人士何阿芳（Woo Ah Yong）的陈述，由本人 D.P.S. Jones 于1932年10月17日在总部录取，并由职员陈洪（Chen Hung）翻译。

我叫何阿芳，又名何芳，又名何子锦（Woo Ts King），26岁，浙江籍，已婚。我的籍贯是温州附近的瑞安县岩川村（Mienchmen village, Zae An Hsien）。14岁之前，我在乡村塾师处学习中文。
随后我进入温州的一所师范学校，在那里学习了4年半。毕业后，我在家乡的一所小学教了一年书。我在上海有一位名叫金先生（King Zah Sung）的朋友，邀请我去与他共事。于是我于1926年6月前往上海。金先生在国民党上海区党部担任秘书。我在闸北他的家中协助他，印刷国民党的文件和信件。1927年2月，我在闸北上海大学遇到了学生金华韩（King Mo Han）。此人属于共产党交通局。结识他后不久，我加入了该党，并被交通局聘为信使，月薪25元。当时我仍在为金先生（King Zah Sung）工作，并与他同住在闸北。1927年9月，共产党派我前往莫斯科东方大学。我在那里学习了一年，随后转入同一城市的孙逸仙大学，在那里学习了两年共产主义理论。离开大学后的6个月里，我在莫斯科的一家红色政治工厂担任铜匠。在这段时期结束时，我被迫离开该国

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Wong Chien Jong
native of Lingtsu, Shantung. taken by me D. S Jones
at H'quarters on the 17/10/32 and interpreted by Liao Tsong Chien

My name is Wong Chien Jong (王鑑堂), alias Wong Liang
Tung (王良棟), 28 years, married, native of Lingtsu (子口)
Shantung. My home address is Wong Kia Ling (黃家嶺), Lingtsu,
Shantung.

At the age of 12 years I entered the Tse Liang (朱良)
Primary School, which is about ten li from Lingtsu. After three
years at this school I went to the 10th Middle School, founded
by Shantung Province. Owing to the poverty of my family I had
to leave school altogether a year later and return home to
assist my father and grand-father in running the farm. I
remained on the farm until three years ago, when I came to
Shanghai, bringing with me various goods from the Northern
Provinces, which I intended selling here. This venture proved
a failure and I lost about $3000.00.

In June 1931 I opened an exchange shop at 22 Chien Yih Li
(建義里), Route Frelupt, in the French Concession, which I
am still managing. The following month one Sih Kung Siao (施公孝)
who was then dwelling in the Chien Yih Li Alleyway opened an
account at my shop. In July 1932 he left for Pootoo, owing me
approximately $20.00. As security for the debt he left behind four
wooden boxes. I did not know what they contained until the Police
came to my shop and opened them in my presence at 11 p.m. on
October 15.

I am not a communist and do not belong to any party. I
always knew Sih Kung Pao as a merchant and never knew that he
had any interest in Communism.

(Signed) Wong Chien Jong.

以下为山东岭子（Lingtsu）籍人士王鉴堂（Wong Chien Jong）的陈述，由本人 D. S Jones 于1932年10月17日在总部录取，并由廖宗建（Liao Tsong Chien）翻译。

我叫王鉴堂，又名王良栋（Wong Liang Tung），28岁，已婚，山东岭子（子口）人。我的家庭住址是山东岭子黄家岭（Wong Kia Ling）。

12岁时，我进入距离岭子约十里的朱良（Tse Liang）小学。在该校就读三年后，我进入山东省立第十中学。由于家境贫寒，一年后我不得不完全辍学，回家协助父亲和祖父经营农场。我在农场一直待到三年前，当时我来到上海，带来了各种北方省份的货物，打算在此出售。这次尝试失败了，我损失了约3000.00美元。

1931年6月，我在法租界贝勒路（Route Frelupt）建义里22号开了一家兑换店，目前仍由我经营。次月，当时住在建义里弄堂的施公孝（Sih Kung Siao）在我的店里开了一个账户。1932年7月，他前往普陀，欠我约20.00美元。作为债务担保，他留下了四个木箱。直到10月15日晚上11点警察来到我的店里并在我面前打开箱子时，我才知道里面装的是什么。

我不是共产党员，也不属于任何党派。我一直知道施公保（Sih Kung Pao，注：此处原文名字拼写与前文施公孝略有不同，依原文译出）是一名商人，从不知道他对共产主义有任何兴趣。

（签名）王鉴堂（Wong Chien Jong）。

Copy of an extract from the "Chinese Workers Correspondence",
Vol.4, No.33, dated August 30, 1934.

CHINESE TROTSKISTS OPENLY BACK KMT

In China there is now more evidence to confirm the
counterrevolutionary character of the Trotskists in China.
Chen Tu-shu, Pen Shu-tse and a dozen others who call them-
selves Trotskists have openly gone over to the side of the
KMT bandits by a further betrayal to the working class of
China.

At a retrial taking place recently in Nanking Chen
and Pen openly declared that the red army of the Soviets
is nothing but 'bandits and tramps', that the red army is
unnecessary at present, to be organised according to their
opinion only after the formation of the Soviets, a theory
that had long been preached by these counterrevolutionaries
but sneered at by the working masses.

Chen et Als 'Arrested'

It shall be recalled that Chen et als, self-styled
leaders of Trotskism in China, were 'arrested' in 1932, just at t
the moment when the Kuomintang bandits withdrew their troops
from the anti-Japanese front and directed them against the
red army in Hupeh-Hunan-Anhwei. The KMT bandits 'arrested'
them because they needed more than ever the services of the
Chinese Trotskists. During the ensuing trial Chen and Pen
bravely fought for the Kuomintang bandits exactly in the same
way as the bandit leader Chiang Kai-shek fought the red
armies at the front. In opening the campaign Chen and Pen
fired hot shots at the red army and Soviets by saying that
the name of red army is only a camouflage for bandits and
tramps, that there is no need for the red army. The
bourgeois press and KMT news agency fully utilized these
shots of the Trotskists to re-enforce their red-suppressing
campaign in the newspapers and journals. But, in fact, the
4th KMT campaign broke down before the onslaught of the red
army which grew out of the land revolution. Far from being
bandits and tramps, the red army has become the main
defensive force of the Soviet regime in China. These clear
facts are a direct contradiction of the lies and slanders of
the Chinese Trotskists.

Needless to say, the Trotskists arraigned were treated
as guests of Honor in the KMT prison. They have been living
on the hospitality of the KMT bandits for almost two years,
busying themselves with writing of articles and pamphlets
for the furtherance of the KMT cause of capitulation and
oppression. Chen wrote a book for Chiang Kai-shek entitled
'the Red Army' amplifying and illustrating his theory (theory
of considering the red army as bandits and tramps) with fresh
lies and slanders. The pamphlet is prefaced by Chiang Kai-
shek.

Chen's New Job

Chen's job is now of greater importance under new
conditions. With the proclamation of the armed self defence
by the Chinese people, with the dispatch of the anti-Japanese
vanguard by the Soviet government of China, with the sweeping
successes of the red army in Fukien, the KMT bandits feel
more menaced than ever and attempt to mobilise all the forces
for defence.

《中国工人通讯》第4卷第33期（1934年8月30日出版）摘录副本。

中国托洛茨基派公开支持国民党

在中国，现在有越来越多的证据证实中国托洛茨基派的反革命性质。陈独秀、彭述之以及十余名自称为托洛茨基派的人，通过进一步背叛中国工人阶级，已公开投奔国民党匪帮一方。

在南京最近进行的一次复审中，陈和彭公开宣称，苏维埃红军不过是“匪徒和流浪汉”，认为目前不需要红军，按照他们的观点，红军只有在苏维埃成立之后才需要组织。这一理论早已被这些反革命分子所宣扬，但受到广大劳动群众的嘲笑。

陈等人被“逮捕”

回顾往事，自称是中国托洛茨基主义领导人的陈独秀等人于1932年被“逮捕”，那正是国民党匪帮从抗日前线撤军并将兵力调往鄂豫皖地区进攻红军的时刻。国民党匪帮“逮捕”他们，是因为他们比以往任何时候都更需要中国托洛茨基派的服务。在随后的审判中，陈和彭以与匪首蒋介石在前线进攻红军完全相同的方式，勇敢地为国民党匪帮效力。在发起这场攻势时，陈和彭向红军和苏维埃发射了“重磅炮弹”，声称红军之名只是匪徒和流浪汉的伪装，没有必要存在红军。资产阶级报刊和国民党通讯社充分利用了托洛茨基派的这些言论，在报纸和期刊上加强其镇压红色的宣传运动。然而，事实上，国民党的第四次围剿在源于土地革命的红军猛攻下破产了。红军绝非匪徒和流浪汉，而已成为中国苏维埃政权的主要防御力量。这些清楚的事实直接驳斥了中国托洛茨基派的谎言和诽谤。

不用说，受审的托洛茨基派在国民党监狱中被当作贵宾对待。他们在国民党匪帮的款待下生活了近两年，忙于撰写文章和小册子，以推进国民党投降和压迫的事业。陈为蒋介石写了一本书，题为《红军》，用新的谎言和诽谤来扩充和阐释他的理论（即视红军为匪徒和流浪汉的理论）。该书由蒋介石作序。

陈的新工作

在新形势下，陈的工作变得更为重要。随着中国人民宣布武装自卫，随着中华苏维埃政府派遣抗日先锋部队，以及红军在福建取得的全面胜利，国民党匪帮感到前所未有的威胁，并试图动员一切力量进行防御。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Just this moment Chen and other Trotskists come out
in the open to support the Kuomintang. Under the pretext
of taking an appeal to the ●supreme court at Nanking Chen
and his company denounced the anti-Japanese crusade of the
red army by repeating the old slander, and stood solidly
behind the KMT bandits for surrender and capitulation. On
August 11 the Shanghai press featured the decision handed
down by the supreme court on Chen's appeal, giving prominence
to that passage of the verdict which quotes Chen's denunciation
of the red army as bandits and tramps.

Another passage of the verdict says, "Chen & Co. are
rather erudited scholars in view of their objection to the
peasant rioting led by the Stalinists with the help of
bandits and disarmed soldiers. They have not the slightest
egotism (?)". The court rewarded the acts of the Trotskists
by reducing the sentence from 13 years to 8 years, restoring
the civil rights deprived by the lower court, etc.

The gentlemanly treatment given to the Chinese
Trotskists contrasts sharply with that accorded to the
genuine revolutionaries, the communists and their allies
who are subject to all sorts of torture invented by modern
genius, for the simple reason that the Chinese Trotskists
are followers of the KMT bandits on the political front.

While the whole country is raising the clamour for
the speedy overthrow of the KMT traitors, Chinese Trotskists
loudly shout the last slogan in defence of the shaken KMT
bandits, a fact that proves beyond all doubt the real
counterrevolutionary physiognomy of Chinese Trotskists.

page_data.zh:
- 2 -

就在此时，陈和其他托洛茨基派公开站出来支持国民党。借口向南京●最高法院上诉，陈及其同伙重弹旧调，诋毁红军的抗日 crusade（圣战/讨伐），并坚定地站在国民党匪帮一边，主张投降和屈服。8月11日，上海报刊重点报道了最高法院对陈上诉案作出的判决，突出强调了判决书中引用陈指责红军为匪徒和流浪汉的那一段落。

判决书的另一段写道：“鉴于陈等人反对斯大林分子在匪徒和解散士兵的帮助下领导的农民暴动，他们可谓是学识渊博的学者。他们毫无自私之心（？）”。法院通过减轻刑罚来奖励托洛茨基派的行为，将刑期从13年减至8年，恢复了下级法院剥夺的公民权利等。

给予中国托洛茨基派的绅士待遇，与给予真正的革命者、共产党人及其盟友的待遇形成鲜明对比，后者遭受现代天才发明的各种酷刑，原因很简单，中国托洛茨基派在政治战线上是国民党匪帮的追随者。

当全国上下都在高声呼吁迅速推翻国民党叛徒时，中国托洛茨基派却大声喊出保卫摇摇欲坠的国民党匪帮的最后口号，这一事实无可辩驳地证明了中国托洛茨基派真正的反革命面目。

COPY OF EXTRACT OF NEWSPAPER TRANSLATION OF JULY 21, 1934.

THE CASE AGAINST CHEN TOU SEU AND OTHERS

Eastern Times (Nanking Telegram) and other local newspapers :

The Supreme Court has handed down the following
decision in the appeal filed by Chen Tou Seu, Bang Jih Tse
(陳独秀，彭述之 ) and others :

"The original sentence passed on Chen Tou
Seu and Bang Jih Tse and the deprivation of civil rights
of Wong Wu (王武 ), Po Ih Vai (濮一凡 ), Wong Zao Chung
(王兆羣 ) and Kwoh Han Hao (郭漢豪 ) are hereby cancelled.
Chen Tou Seu and Bang Jih Tse are sentenced to 8 years
imprisonment each for activities against the security
of the State. Every two days imprisonment before the
present judgment will be counted as one day's imprisonment.
The literature and other documents seized in connection
with the case are to be confiscated."

Chen Tou Seu and Bang Jih Tse were sentenced
each to 15 years imprisonment by the Kiangsu High Court.
As a result of their appeal, their sentence has now
been reduced. They have been in prison for over one year.
